Brighton midfielder Malick Yalcouye face a lengthy spell on the sidelines due to a knee injury.

The Ivory Coast star sustained the injury while on international and missed last Sunday’s 2-0 Premier League loss at Hull City.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Head coach Fabian Hurzeler confirmed that Yalcouye is now ruled out of Thursday’s Uefa Conference League clash against Romanian League leaders Craiova and could be out for a ”several weeks.”.

“Several weeks, definitely,” confirmed the Albion boss. “It could be anywhere from six to 10 weeks, so unfortunately it's a long-term injury.

“But I think he's a quick healer and he will come back as swiftly as possible.”.

Sources indicate that the Ivory Coast midfielder has made 17 appearances in all competitions during the 2026/27 campaign, scoring four goals and providing no assists. His Premier League contribution stands at 10 appearances and two goals, while he has also found the net in the Conference League and Carabao Cup.

The 21-year-old has particularly impressed with his energy, athleticism and willingness to drive forward from midfield.

Industry observers note that hurzeler added: “Of course, every injury hurts us because we feel for the player. We build relationships with the players, and every player wants to be on the pitch and express themselves on the pitch. If they can't do that, you feel for them.

“I think that's the worst thing that can happen to a player: being injured, being out and seeing their teammates performing on the pitch from the sidelines.

”We have a great environment where we can really help these players and give them the belief that they can come back as quickly as possible. That's also what we're doing with Malick.”.

Elsewhere, Diego Gomez will be rested against Craiova while Olivier Boscagli misses out due to illness. Left back Jaouen Hadjam is out due to injury and the match will also arrive too soon for Stefanos Tzimas.

In a recent development, “Yes, too soon [for Tzimas] mentioned Hurzeler to Sussex World. “I think his first step will be a game with the Under-21s, and then we'll go from there.

“But, as I remarked at the last press conference, it's a joy to see him training, and huge credit to him so far.”.

On Hadjam, Hurzeler remarked: “Hadjim has a small issue, definitely a small issue, but we have to take it day by day.

Industry observers note that “I just spoke to him and he feels quite confident. He has a lot of trust in his body. For tomorrow it's too early, but hopefully he'll be available for Sunday.”.

On the plus side, summer signing Femi Azeez is fit and could make his debut on Thursday night.

Juventus vs Omonia - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (666 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jonathan O'Shea | 24 Nov 2026 15:08, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 15:10.
  • Seeking to extend their unbeaten run through this season's Europa League, Juventus will welcome Omonia to Turin on Thursday evening.
  • While Juve are on track for automatic qualification to the last 16, their visitors are bound for the knockout playoffs as things stand.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 24 Nov 2026 15:08, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 15:10.

Seeking to extend their unbeaten run through this season's Europa League, Juventus will welcome Omonia to Turin on Thursday evening.

While Juve are on track for automatic qualification to the last 16, their visitors are bound for the knockout playoffs as things stand.

More accustomed to Champions League football, Juventus have made a strong start to their campaign in Europe's second tier, claiming 10 points from a possible 12 so far.

After a 5-0 cruise at home to NEC, the Italian giants secured victory over Celta Vigo on matchday two, before playing out a 2-2 draw against Rennes.

Last time out, they retained a top-eight spot by beating AZ in Alkmaar, where Teun Koopmeiners scored against his former club in a tense 2-1 win.

Since then, results have somewhat improved in Serie A, after Juve had made an inconsistent start; four points from two games have lifted Luciano Spalletti's side up to sixth place.

Having fought back twice to salvage a draw with Fiorentina, they then put four goals past lowly Venezia, inspired by Nick Woltemade's half-time introduction from the bench.

However, Spalletti's injury-hit squad still trail 11 points behind league leaders Lazio, while Italy's tight top-four fight could go all the way.

Before facing fellow contenders Como on Sunday, Juve will aim to maintain their undefeated home record in the Europa League, having won six games and drawn nine in Turin since the competition began.

Juventus have also won all four prior meetings with Omonia Nicosia, beating them over two legs in both the 1977-78 European Cup and the 1999-00 UEFA Cup - the Cypriot side lost 10-2 on the latter occasion.

While Juve sit fifth in the Europa League table on 10 points, Omonia's tally of six leaves them 18th midway through the league phase, so defeat could see them drop into the elimination zone.

After coming through qualifying, then winning two of their first three games, Henning Berg's side suffered a 3-1 defeat to NEC on matchday four, despite seizing the lead through Lois Diony's opening goal.

Since that setback, they have beaten Anorthosis Famagusta and drawn 1-1 with city rivals APOEL, with Diony scoring on both occasions. As a result, the Nicosia club are fifth in the Cypriot top flight, five points shy of the summit.

Their domestic title defence may not be going to strategy, but Omonia are on track to escape a Europa League group or league phase for the first time to date - albeit potentially via the playoffs.

Juventus form (all competitions):.

Juventus still have a long absence list, and Kerim Alajbegovic is set to join it on Thursday evening, after picking up a minor thigh problem against Venezia.

Pierre Kalulu and Nico Gonzalez are expected to return from injury this weekend, but Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram, Kamil Grabara and captain Manuel Locatelli are still sidelined.

Newcastle United loanee Woltemade now has nine goal contributions for the Bianconeri, having either scored or assisted in all four Europa League appearances.

Likely to support Randal Kolo Muani up front, the German striker also ranks second for shots attempted and for open-play chances created in this season's league phase.

Meanwhile, French forward Diony should lead Omonia's attack, after scoring in three consecutive matches.

Though Hungary international Loic Nego recently returned from a layoff, Carel Eiting is still ruled out by a long-term knee injury.

Juventus possible starting lineup:.

Vicario; Celik, Gatti, Bremer, Cabal; Sarr, Koopmeiners; Conceicao, Woltemade, Boga; Kolo Muani.

Omonia possible starting lineup:.

Kaminski; Mayambela, Coulibaly, Satka, Duverne; Andreou, Maric; Ewandro, Tanase, Montnor; Diony.

Both sides have scored in every league-phase game, and the evidence suggests that trend should continue.

Juventus may be fallen giants but they are still too strong for most opponents at this level - and particularly when playing on home turf.

It was reported on Saturday, October 31 that a cup tie between two West Sussex Football League teams was abandoned after an incident which left a player needing to go to hospital with serious mouth and jaw injuries.

Midhurst & Easebourne Community were playing a home Malcolm Simmonds Memorial Cup match at the Rotherfield against Emsworth Town when the flashpoint occurred around 15 minutes into the match.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Midhurst & Easebourne FC stated at the time two of their players were assaulted by someone from the opposition team, with one going to hospital.

Police and league officials have been involved as investigations continue – with the club saying they are doing all they can to support ‘one of our own’ at a ‘horrific’ time.

Sussex Police confirmed an investigation into the incident had been launched on November 2.

And in their latest patch, the force confirmed the investigation was still ongoing.

A Sussex Police spokesperson stated on Wednesday (November 25): “There is no current revision. The investigation is ongoing.”.

Town revealed Macdonald’s departure on Saturday night with the team second from bottom of the Isthmian SE division – but the decision has provoked an angry and disbeliving response from many players, while a number of players and volunteers have since left the club.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Macdonald told us he had been told eight days before being sacked his job was ‘bomb-proof’ and he had still not been given a reason for his removal.

Although Town are in the relegation zone they have had a horrendous run of injuries and have shown signs of better results with draws in their past two games, including a creditable 0-0 draw at home to Whitstable last Saturday, Macdonald and Ben Davis’s last game at the helm.

In a recent development, but Town have now publicised the vacant role. They remarked: “Eastbourne Town FC is seeking a dedicated, ambitious and committed First Team Manager to lead the club into its next chapter.

"We are looking for an individual who shares our ambition, understands the importance of building a strong club culture and is passionate about developing players, creating opportunities and delivering success both on and off the pitch.

Sources indicate that “The successful candidate will be someone who: Has a clear football philosophy, strong leadership qualities and the ability to motivate and develop players. Is committed to building a competitive, hard-working and united first-team squad. Recognises the importance of developing young talent and creating a clear pathway from youth football into senior football. Is enthusiastic about developing our U18 and U23 football programmes, ensuring talented young players are given genuine opportunities to progress into the First Team. Is prepared to work collaboratively with the club’s youth coaches and wider football management team. Can build positive relationships with players, volunteers, supporters and the wider club community. Demonstrates professionalism, integrity, commitment and a strong desire to represent Eastbourne Town FC with pride.

"Building for the Future: At Eastbourne Town, we believe the First Team should be an vital part of a wider football development pathway.

“We want to create an environment where young players can see a realistic route from youth football through U18 and U23 football and ultimately into the First Team.

"We are looking for a manager who embraces this philosophy, is willing to invest time in developing young players and understands that giving opportunities to homegrown talent can be just as vital as recruiting established players.

In a recent development, “This does not mean compromising ambition or competitiveness. We want to build a team capable of competing, progressing and achieving success while developing the next generation of Eastbourne Town players.

“Our Vision: We want a manager who wants to be part of something bigger than just managing a Saturday afternoon team. Someone who wants to build, develop and contribute to the long-term future of Eastbourne Town FC.

“If you have the passion, leadership, experience and ambition to take our First Team forward while helping shape the future of football at our club, we would love to hear from you.

"Please send applications to the Director of Football – [email protected] – the closing date for applications is 1st December 2026. Eastbourne Town FC – Building for Today, Developing for Tomorrow.”.

Claude, find me a planet: amateur astronomers are using AI with mixed results

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (817 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Artificial-intelligence tools are helping citizen scientists to find undiscovered exoplanets (artist’s illustration).Credit: Hypersphere/SPL.
  • In September, Pavel Rabtsevich sat down at his computer and asked an AI model to discover a planet.
  • History’s long-secret codes are being cracked by amateurs using AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Artificial-intelligence tools are helping citizen scientists to find undiscovered exoplanets (artist’s illustration).Credit: Hypersphere/SPL.

In September, Pavel Rabtsevich sat down at his computer and asked an AI model to discover a planet. Rabtsevich directed the program to a specific batch of telescope data and gave it a high-level plan to hunt for evidence of undetected planets. In about two weeks, the program delivered the goods: two possible planets orbiting a star 116 light years from Earth. Professional astronomers are now checking the findings.

History’s long-secret codes are being cracked by amateurs using AI.

History’s long-secret codes are being cracked by amateurs using AI.

Rabtsevich, who works in Spain as an artificial-intelligence specialist and has no formal astronomy education, is one of the most successful of a wave of amateur astronomers who are using AI models to search for worlds outside the Solar System. Citizen scientists have been using publicly available tools from NASA and other researchers to find planets for decades. But AI’s ability to scour the Internet for such tools and use them to process massive amounts of data has lowered the barrier to entry for non-specialists who want to become planet hunters.

Recent findings suggest that the newfound accessibility of data-analysis tools, however, has meant that not all amateurs are doing research responsibly, claims Michelle Kunimoto, an exoplanet researcher at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver, Canada. Some planet hunters don’t fully understand the algorithms being used by AI tools and thus can’t validate the models’ findings, Kunimoto says. “There’s been a huge, overwhelming surge of AI-driven papers, which tend to have [planet] candidates that are not the best quality,” they say. And as a result, “the systems we use to disseminate science are being overwhelmed”.

For his search, Rabtsevich enlisted Claude Code, an AI coding tool made by Anthropic. He asked it to sift through data from more than 120,000 stars observed by NASA’s Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) in late 2025 and early 2026. He guided Claude to use a popular planet-detection algorithm to search for dips in the stars’ brightness. A regular and repeated dimming of a star can be a sign that a planet is orbiting it and blocking a little bit of light every time it passes between the star and an observer.

According to recent reports, claude zeroed in on a star called TIC 4206066, which showed two separate cycles of dimming, one roughly every 3 days and another every 11 days. That suggests that TIC 4206066 is orbited by two planets, one of which loops around the star more tightly than the other and thus takes less time to complete a full rotation.

These alien planets are astronomers’ favourites.

These alien planets are astronomers’ favourites.

It has been revealed that rabtsevich instructed Claude to look for those same repetitive patterns in archival TESS data. Sure enough, data from 2018 and 2020 recorded the same pattern of dimming coming from TIC 4206066. At Rabtsevich’s direction, Claude then found a planet-detection algorithm, one written and made publicly available by Kunimoto, and ran it to validate the signals.

Rabtsevich published his findings to the platform Zenodo as a preprint1 on 25 September. His work has not been peer reviewed, but TESS astronomers have completed an independent analysis of the signals and have added them to their official list of planet candidates.

Olympiacos vs AC Milan - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (748 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jonathan O'Shea | 24 Nov 2026 16:29, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 11:32.
  • Ailing giants AC Milan must try to kickstart their Europa League campaign on Thursday evening, when they visit Olympiacos at the Georgios Karaiskakis Stadium.
  • Despite their status as seven-time European champions, Milan are on course for early elimination, while their unbeaten hosts have only dropped two points so far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 24 Nov 2026 16:29, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 11:32.

Ailing giants AC Milan must try to kickstart their Europa League campaign on Thursday evening, when they visit Olympiacos at the Georgios Karaiskakis Stadium.

Despite their status as seven-time European champions, Milan are on course for early elimination, while their unbeaten hosts have only dropped two points so far.

Milan will head into the second half of the league phase with a point to prove, having lost three out of four games to date - including the last two without scoring.

Recently beaten by Bournemouth and Ferencvaros, Ruben Amorim's side have failed to even find the scoresheet since Goncalo Ramos struck in their lone win against Red Bull Salzburg.

A paltry tally of three points leaves the Italian heavyweights in real danger of being knocked out, as they sit 28th in the Europa League table and only the top 24 will go through.

By contrast with their continental results, Milan are showing clear signs of progress in Serie A, where they occupy fourth place, just ahead of city rivals and reigning champions Inter.

The Rossoneri have taken 15 points from the last available 18 - while scoring at least twice on each occasion - and they have only lost one domestic fixture this term.

Aiming to keep pace in the Scudetto race, Amorim's men hosted surprise high-flyers Frosinone last weekend, when they eventually cruised to a 5-1 win, with rising star Alphadjo Cisse scoring again.

However, Milan must now head to Greece, where they memorably won the 1994 Champions League final but have never beaten native hosts in six prior attempts.

In particular, Milan's two previous visits to Piraeus ended with a 2-2 draw in 1959 and a 3-1 defeat in 2018, when Olympiacos won the most recent meeting.

That was also in the Europa League, and the Greek giants currently sit sixth in this season's league phase - seven points clear of the Rossoneri.

As things stand, Olympiacos will directly enter the last 16, despite losing their perfect record last time out.

Across all competitions, they had won nine straight games before being held to a 0-0 draw by Rennes, which followed victories over Jagiellonia Bialystok, Marseille and Sparta Prague.

All told, Imanol Alguacil's side have lost just one of their last 18 fixtures, and Sunday's 6-2 destruction of 10-man Iraklis left them second in the Greek Super League standings.

Furthermore, Olympiacos have only suffered one defeat in their last 13 Europa League matches - while keeping nine clean sheets - so they will surely fear no-one on home turf.

Olympiacos form (all competitions):.

AC Milan form (all competitions):.

Amorim has typically shuffled his lineup for Europa League games - albeit not to positive effect - and several fringe players should feature for Milan.

Omari Hutchinson and Ardon Jashari have often played, while Cisse could start again; the new Italy international already has six Serie A goals and he scored a hat-trick away to Salzburg earlier in the campaign.

At the other end of the spectrum, experienced captain Mike Maignan can return after serving a one-match ban for his red card against Bournemouth.

Goncalo Ramos is set to overcome a minor calf problem, but the visitors must travel without Mattia Gabbia, Fikayo Tomori, Samuel Chukwueze, Alexis Saelemaekers and Ruben Loftus-Cheek due to injury.

Meanwhile, Olympiacos are missing long-term absentees Ayoub El Kaabi and Yusuf Yazici, plus South American pair Gustavo Puerta and Santiago Hezze.

Leon Bailey bagged two goals and an assist at the weekend, so he could link up with Armando Gonzalez, who is the hosts' top Europa League scorer with two.

Portuguese playmaker Jota Silva has racked up the most shots in this season's league phase; however, just two of those 17 attempts have found the target and none have hit the net.

Olympiacos possible starting lineup:.

Ortega; Saliakas, Retsos, Carmo, Onyemaechi; Freuler, Scipioni; Bailey, Silva, Fortounis; Gonzalez.

AC Milan possible starting lineup:.

Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Pavlovic, Diawara; Musah, Jashari; Hutchinson, Rabiot, Cisse; Ramos.

Milan may have struggled to score in Europe, but with Amorim developing an exciting front line, they average above two goals per game in Serie A and are overdue to convert some chances.

That said, Olympiacos are a formidable force on home soil, so they can keep their unbeaten streak going with a hard-fought draw.

By Darren Plant | 24 Nov 2026 16:33, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 16:47.

Unai Emery has made four changes to his starting lineup for Tuesday's Champions League fixture against Galatasaray.

With the condition of the RAMS Park preventing Villa from training on the surface on Monday, it felt plausible that Emery could protect some of his star players.

Instead, barring the exclusion of Pau Torres and Emiliano Buendia, the Spaniard has arguably named the strongest lineup from the options available to him.

Taylor Harwood-Bellis has moved over to right-back to replace Aaron Wan-Bissaka, with Tyrone Mings getting the nod over Torres in the middle.

Joao Gomes has returned to the midfield in place of Leon Goretzka, while John McGinn returns ahead of Buendia.

Nicolas Jackson has retained his place down the middle of the attack, with former Besiktas frontman Tammy Abraham among the substitutes.

Chelsea loanee Alejandro Garnacho has again been left out of the Villa squad.

Meanwhile, Okan Buruk has recalled the likes of former Tottenham Hotspur defender Davinson Sanchez and ex-Wolverhampton Wanderers midfielder Mario Lemina to his Galatasaray XI.

Former Arsenal man Lucas Torreira is another ex-Premier League player to be selected in the team.

However, former Norwich City star Gabriel Sara has dropped down to the substitutes' bench, joining Leroy Sane.

Lesley Ugochukwu - on loan from Burnley - is also kept in reserve, but top goalscorer Victor Osimhen remains sidelined through injury.

Galatasaray XI: Ugurcan; Singo, Sanchez, Bardakci, Jakobs; Torreira, Lemina, Elmali; Akgun, Batrakov, Yilmaz.

Subs: Bitshiabu, Sara, Gul, Gundogan, Guvenc, Lus, Nhaga, Sane, Ugochukwu, Yilmaz.

Aston Villa XI: Suzuki; Harwood-Bellis, Lindelof, Mings, Maatsen; Kamara, Gomes; Alysson, McGinn, Manzambi; Jackson.

Subs: Bizot, Wright, Barkley, Buendia, Torres, Abraham, Mbaye, Bogarde, Goretzka, Wan-Bissaka, Hemmings.

Manager Chris Wilder cannot wait.

According to recent reports, after a difficult summer transfer window, his side took time to get but are now hitting their stride, with four wins in the last six matches. It feels like they might be ready to take on some of the best teams in the division at the best time of the season to get some momentum.

"I don't get fazed by that," noted Wilder of the fixture list awaiting his side.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

According to recent reports, "I think sometimes they're the better games for us, where teams have to come out and open up and they are really good teams. QPR (who the Blades play away on Saturday) are playing really well. Southampton are a top side.

"Whatever happened last season, whatever opinion you've got on it (Spygate, which saw them expelled from the Championship play-offs), they would have gone up.

"I know you can't absolutely guarantee it, sometimes these things are not meant to be in the play-offs but I just think that the way they were steamrolling teams at the back end of last season, the way they dealt with Middlesbrough in the play-offs, I think they would have dealt with Hull City in my opinion.

“Not absolute guarantees because things can happen in football. But they would have been a Premier League team this season.

"I like the manager (former Barnsley coach Tonda Eckert), I think he's a really good football manager, and they've got top players.

"They've got good experience – Championship players and players that have played in the Premier League.

"Everybody looks at the fixtures and says, 'You have to deal with them' and 'That's easy.'.

Industry observers note that "They're not sometimes the easy games. Go and ask Southampton when they played Preston and they get turned over. Go and ask Middlesbrough when they draw at Watford. Preston get a result at West Ham.

"That's the nature of the division.

"But we're looking forward to these substantial home games.

In a recent development, "Southampton at home – brilliant game for us. West Ham at home – brilliant game for us. Middlesbrough coming to Bramall Lane, Burnley coming to Bramall Lane, some top sides coming to play.

"We'll have the utmost respect for all those sides.

"And I don't think any of those sides will be thinking, 'Well, Sheffield United are just one of those teams that we can easily turn over.'.

"Hopefully the crowd see it and smell it and sense it as well and give us the backing that I believe we need on Tuesday night and at times deserve.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The South Shields-born player has plied his trade out east at Norwich City and Peterborough United and also way out west at Plymouth Argyle.

It's been quite a journey and now he finds himself back a fair bit closer to his native north east at Huddersfield Town, settled both on and off the pitch.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Not that his initial few months in West Yorkshire were particularly easy.

January moves are often not straightforward and so it proved for the left-sided player.

He joined a Town side wrestling with form issues - a few hours after he made his debut, Lee Grant was sacked - and the mood in the stands hardly improved as winter turned to spring.

Thankfully, the mood music is transformed these days at second-placed Town, who visit Doncaster Rovers in a Yorkshire derby on Thursday evening.

Mumba, whose partner had a baby earlier this year, said: "My family have all settled. My missus, the kids, my daughters, they're all good.

Recent findings suggest that "I've settled. This is home. Obviously, it's not far from where my actual family live, which is up north in Newcastle.

"Everything now, for me, is where I need it to be. I'm exactly where I feel like I'm meant to be at this point in my career.

"I think I was closer to France when I was at Plymouth than actually to my family up north!. I've been all over the place. I started off at Sunderland and went to Norwich, Peterborough and Plymouth.

"It's been quite a journey, to be fair. It's finally good to be in the middle, at the centre of everything and have the support that I have closer to me and around me.

"I also had pre-season to help me find my focus and concentration and really start again and start reaping the rewards.".

Mumba is starting to display the form which convinced Town to shelve out a significant fee of around £1million to bring him back north in the January window.

A fan favourite during his time at Home Park, Mumba played a major part in Argyle's League One title-winning campaign in 2022-23.

Highlights included a superb solo goal in the Devonians' first game back in the second-tier after a 13-year absence in August 2023 - ironically against Town.

Mumba, who signed a long-term deal with Town until at least 2029, is now chasing a second promotion from the third tier - in the blue and white of Town as opposed to the green and white of Argyle.

Sources indicate that he continued: "Right now, I would say I'm getting that vibe that I got from Plymouth. For me, it's the dressing room, players and togetherness that gives you the success.

"At Norwich, it was the same. The year we got promoted at (Plymouth), I feel like that togetherness was really what was behind the success, what a lot of people don't see. Come Saturday, you're going to war with your mate.

It has been revealed that "Whoever's next to you, you're going into the battle. You've got to have that relationship and you've got to care for each other.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan put on a show at San Siro on Sunday night as they swept Frosinone aside emphatically, beating them 5-1.

It has been revealed that the own-goal that Gabriele Calvani scored a few minutes in set the tone for the visitors, while Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack. However, Patrizio Masini’s goal shortly after meant the deficit was halved going into the break.

It has been revealed that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the second half, Milan ran riot. Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse both had opportunities after being found in behind, and both just minutes after coming off the bench. Then, Christian Pulisic added the finishing touch to make it a five-star night.

Recent findings suggest that it was a win that Milan needed, considering that only Inter out of the current top six, dropped points, and it moves the Rossoneri back into the top four spots. Ivan Stoev has picked out the key talking points from the game.

Technically, Rabiot won the MOTM in our post-game ratings, but we absolutely have to talk about Luka Modric.

According to recent reports, I’ve personally had my doubts about the Croatian being able to keep up this season, especially under Ruben Amorim. We all expected the Portuguese coach to bring a lot of intensity to Milan’s game and at times, Modric has seemed to struggle.

Maybe that was because of the team adapting to the latest coach, or maybe the midfielder hadn’t completely recovered after the World Cup – who knows.

The reality is that the former Real Madrid man has stepped up after some shaky games at the start of the season and continues to prove his quality on and off the ball and his athleticism and longevity are nothing short of extraordinary.

According to recent reports, the vision and passing ability to play the through ball to Rabiot for the opening goal was world-class. He then continued to dictate the tempo and make impressive forward runs, playing the full 90 minutes, giving it his all until the final whistle.

The management really needs to assemble a whole group of people tasked to find a proper replacement for Modric, as he will leave a big gap in that midfield.

To continue with the midfielder theme, we also have to give praise to Rabiot, who has been absolutely brilliant this season. Don’t get me wrong, he was one of the Rossoneri’s best players last year too.

According to recent reports, yet he has found a higher level since the start of the campaign, as he racked up another two assists and forced the own goal. As a result, he now has five goals and seven assists in 10 games in Serie A – extraordinary numbers.

Sources indicate that on top of the goal contributions, you can count on the Frenchman to be composed under pressure, tidy with his passing, and efficient in both phases of the game. An absolutely stunning start of the season for Rabiot, who is finding new levels to his game under Amorim.

Recent findings suggest that it was such a dominant win that we can probably cover each player and the positives from their game. Nevertheless, one man needs to be praised for sure and that’s Goncalo Ramos, who got himself back on the scoresheet.

Recent findings suggest that needless to say, he opened up a lot of spaces for his teammates and had a role in some of the other goals, which he was doing even when he failed to get the ball in the back of the net. This time around, he also got his long-awaited goal.

It has been revealed that it was a beauty too, in the sense that he dropped deep into his own half, made the tackle to win the ball and kicked off the counter-attack. Following that, he made the run into the opponent’s box and finished it calmly – it was beautifully orchestrated with Ramos in the centre.

The goal and the encouraging performance are also a relief, as we’ve seen many times how strikers struggle to react when they are not scoring, with the confidence level often dropping which results in overall poor form.

However, the Portuguese striker is clearly not in his head and reacted well to a poor spell that spanned both his club and the national team, as he struggled in the international break too.

We didn’t even see that much of him as Amorim subbed him off rather early and it probably has to do with the fact that Milan need a win on Thursday against Olympiacos, in Greece, and Ramos will most likely start the game as the margin for error is little as things stand.

It has been revealed that I mean, what more can you ask from your attackers? Diego Moreira got the hockey assist on the second goal and got an assist for Cisse in the second half and on top of that, was heavily involved and dangerous when the Diavolo went on the counter.

In a recent development, truthfully, the Belgian should have probably scored a goal or two as he had some very good chances in the opponent’s penalty box, but his shooting let him down this time around. Nevertheless, another electric performance.

Speaking of electric – Pulisic also did very well as he was involved in the first goal – even if it ended up being an own goal, his run forced the Frosinone defender to run back and eventually put the ball in his own net.

Industry observers note that the American then got his goal in the second half with a composed finish. He had a very solid game overall with lots of smart movements and combination play- nothing flashy, but the efficiency was there.

Recent findings suggest that then we also have Cisse, who started the game on the bench but only needed nine or so minutes after coming on to get his goal. Ridiculously, he now has six in 10 in the league or a goal every 74 minutes. The youngster made a good run and managed to keep himself onside in a tricky situation and then finished with composure.

The variety in attack by Milan on the night was a joy to watch, as all the players posed a threat to Frosinone, which in the end was too much for them to handle.

Industry observers note that amorim was well aware of how Frosinone would approach the game, which in itself deserves credit as they came to San Siro to play football instead of sitting back. Unfortunately for them and fortunately for us, the coach and his players knew exactly how to get around the high press.

Sources indicate that the Rossoneri were rapid on the counter and created so many chances that the score could’ve easily been even worse for Frosinone. Their high press also didn’t work, as for the majority of the game the Diavolo managed to move the ball around quickly enough, which prevented their opponents from winning it in dangerous areas.

It also must be noted that the Portuguese did well to rest some key players after the third goal, as he will need a fresh lineup for the Europa League fixture on Thursday, where Milan need three points against Olympiacos.

Signed on an initial loan deal until January from Championship club Lincoln City, Collins' long road back to first-team duty—after sustaining a serious knee injury at his parent club almost exactly 12 months ago—meant Rovers had to be patient regarding his availability.

The debut display of the senior striker, who turns 36 on December 1, when he came off the bench midway through the second half in Saturday's draw at Yorkshire rivals Bradford City, also preceded a bit of chatter among Rovers followers.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Collins showed what he was all about, demonstrating his nous to set up Rovers' first equaliser - a brilliant overhead kick from Jordan Thomas - and leading the line in canny fashion.

Given the summer departure of Billy Sharp – a player who similarly brought leadership and nous to the table in the final third – Collins will fill a void in that regard.

The former Republic of Ireland forward has been promoted seven times in his career from the lower leagues with five different clubs – Lincoln, Derby County, Shrewsbury Town, Northampton Town and Luton Town.

There was plenty of noise in the build-up to Saturday from Collins too.

Recent findings suggest that rovers chief Grant McCann revealed: "We've just lacked a little bit of character at times. He's certainly not been quiet on the training ground.

"You can certainly hear the noise levels lift. We did a session (on Friday) on the training pitch and had an 11 v 11 game and Collo was in the team that we were preparing against and he scored against us. And we were like: 'here we go'.

"I could feel the group going a wee bit quiet when we conceded the first goal (at Bradford) and Collo just picked them up and went: ''Lads. I've done this against loads of clubs, so don't be worried'.".

Another welcome returnee was experienced Matty Pearson, who cast aside a booking in the first 25 seconds to stay on message at Valley Parade in only his second league outing of the campaign following injury.

Rovers host Pearson's former club Huddersfield Town on Thursday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two months ago there were many doom merchants insisting that Aston Villa were heading for a season of struggle, but they are looking foolish now.

After a summer of uncertainty and much change, Villa are stepping into a brave new era and find themselves joint-top of the Champions League table after three matches.

With co-owner Nassef Sawiris in attendance, Villa fans are dreaming of another magical season almost four years after Emery walked through the doors at this historic club.

Sawiris was the key figure driving Emery’s appointment in October 2022 and few could have predicted the success that has followed with the Basque manager at the helm.

Villa 2.0 have made a flawless start to their European campaign and are running into form in the Premier League after a sticky start.

In a recent development, in this comfortable victory over Viking, Villa became the second fastest team to win 20 matches at this level from 30 matches, only behind Real Madrid (who won 20 of their first 29). They have also won 12 home games in Europe in a row.

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are presently level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

In a recent development, he stated: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”.

Industry observers note that what a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

It has been revealed that just a week after their biggest European win, the 6-0 destruction of Fenerbahce, expectations were understandably high. Before kick-off a huge tifo was unfurled in the Holte End with the words: “We’ve conquered before. We’re prepared for more.”.

This was not as comfortable but still an impressive performance from this new and exciting team. Alysson, the Brazilian winger, was their man of the match.

Emery had warned his players of complacency against the Norwegian champions, but Villa took command from the start and were ahead after 23 minutes.

Ross Barkley scored twice against Fenerbahce last week and was in the right place again to head Ibrahim Mbaye’s corner past Arild Ostbo.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Champions League fixture as Aston Villa host Viking in the Midlands.

It has been revealed that villa made history in their previous home Champions League outing last week, thrashing Fenerbahce 6-0 to seal the club’s biggest-ever European win. This emphatic victory, coupled with the hard-fought 3-2 triumph over Club Brugge at the start of September, means that Unai Emery’s side have made a 100% winning start to the league phase. The well-deserved 1-0 Premier League victory over Newcastle United at St James’ Park on Saturday evening has amplified the positivity, with Emery’s fresh-look squad beginning to meaningfully gel and now boast a five-match unbeaten streak across all competitions.

Prepared for another night on Europe's biggest stage ✨ https://t.co/oZYiIiGvRg.

Recent findings suggest that despite their Viking’s lack of European pedigree, Villa should be wary of their Norwegian opponents, who secured an unforgettable 3-3 draw with Bayern Munich in Stavanger last time out in the Champions League. The hosts initially flew into a two-goal lead at the break, before a double from Harry Kane and a strike from Luiz Diaz hauled the Bavarians ahead. However, after Michael Olise was sent off, Herman Haugen’s 90th-minute headed equaliser rescued a thrilling draw to give Viking their European point this season following a 3-1 loss to Stuttgart on MD1. Domestically, the reigning champions of Norway are joint top of the Eliteserien with Bodo/Glimt and embroiled in a nailbiting title race with just seven games remaining.

According to recent reports, villa’s injury list includes Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Johan Manzambi, who both picked up issues against Newcastle, as well as Amadou Onana and Matteo Ruggeri. Still, the hosts possess more than enough quality to dismantle Viking, particularly with Nicolas Jackson, who has been in effective form recently and netted a brilliant brace against Fenerbahce.

We’ll bring you the latest updates and drama. Kick-off is at 20:00, with team news coming shortly.

Senegal champions again, but Morocco’s phone call allegation could open a new legal fight

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (732 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Alexis Pereira | 24 Nov 2026 16:33.
  • Senegal have been officially restored as champions of Africa.
  • It is a dramatic twist in a case that had poisoned African football since January.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Alexis Pereira | 24 Nov 2026 16:33.

Senegal have been officially restored as champions of Africa. The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) delivered its verdict on Tuesday 24 November and sided with the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF), overturning the decision by the Confederation of African Football (CAF) that had awarded the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations to Morocco on a technicality. The Lions keep the title they won on the pitch in Rabat.

It is a dramatic twist in a case that had poisoned African football since January. By cancelling the CAF appeal board’s decision of 17 March 2026, CAS sided with the Senegalese federation. The original result of the final is therefore restored: a 1-0 win for Senegal after extra time.

The Lausanne-based court rejected the regulatory reading that had led CAF to penalise the Lions with a forfeit. It found that Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, used by CAF’s appeal committee, were not applicable in this case, and that only the restart of play authorised by the final’s referee, Jean-Jacques Ndala, counted.

‘By blowing his whistle to restart play, the Referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met - both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume,’ the court said. ‘In the Panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee’s decision were limited to the pitch. As such, the Panel considers that the Referee’s decision was covered by the “field of play” doctrine.’.

Sources indicate that the doctrine gives priority to decisions made on the pitch unless there is evidence that the rules were applied arbitrarily or in bad faith. CAS remarked Articles 82 and 84 were only meant to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s behaviour leads the referee to declare that play has definitively stopped, and so did not apply. ‘In conclusion, the panel considers that in resuming the match, the referee did not err in law,’ the court added.

The panel acknowledged that the referee had to decide in a climate of extreme tension, but noted that did not make the decision arbitrary and that his judgement did not appear to have been affected by factors outside the game. On the disciplinary side, it recalled that the FSF, coach Pape Thiaw and some players had already been sanctioned by CAF in separate disciplinary proceedings. The FSF appeal was therefore upheld, and the decision was unanimous.

According to recent reports, on 18 January 2026, Senegal beat Morocco in the final thanks to an extra-time goal from Pape Gueye. Before that goal, the match had turned in stoppage time when referee Ndala awarded Morocco a penalty after a VAR intervention. Furious, coach Thiaw told his players to leave the pitch. After an interruption of around 16 minutes, the Senegalese returned, led by Sadio Mane. Brahim Diaz then missed the Moroccan penalty before Gueye decided the final.

Recent findings suggest that the Moroccan federation (FRMF) immediately contested the match. After its first complaint was rejected by the disciplinary committee, CAF’s appeal board declared Morocco the winners and Senegal forfeited on 17 March, applying Articles 82 and 84 of the competition regulations. The FSF went to CAS on 25 March, and a closed-door hearing took place on 8 October.

The ruling restores Senegal’s status as African champions, giving them a second AFCON after their 2022 triumph in Cameroon. The team, now coached by Patrick Vieira, has two continental titles.

According to recent reports, for Morocco, the verdict is a heavy blow. The host nation, which hoped to win a second crown 50 years after its first in 1976, sees the pitch result confirmed and remains credited with one title. But the case may not have said its last word.

Sources indicate that A few hours before the verdict, the FRMF reported an ‘incident’. According to RMC, the federation denounces an alleged telephone conversation on Sunday between Ulrich Haas, one of the judges appointed to the case, and Abdoulaye Fall, president of the FSF. If proven, that contact could be a flaw Morocco might exploit before the Swiss Federal Tribunal, which can review CAS decisions on procedural grounds.

For its part, CAS says it received no report from Morocco. It remains to be seen whether the controversy marks the start of a newly introduced legal saga.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mullin joined the Bantams on loan from Wrexham in the second half of last season try to push them over the line to promotion but it did not work out as planned for him.

The striker started just two League One games and failed to find the net as Bradford reached the play-offs, but lost in the semi-finals to Bolton Wanderers.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

His next loan, to Rotherham, has been much better for him personally, with eight goals so far, but less so the Millers, who are in the League Two relegation zone after 15 matches. Changing the second half of the equation is about cutting out the mistakes which have bedevilled the team, and 32-year-old Mullin notes he has a major part to play in that.

"I'm really enjoying it," notes Mullin of his time in South Yorkshire.

Recent findings suggest that "I love working with the manager (Alex Bruce) and the players every single day. It's a nice place to be, but t could be a hell of a lot better. We've had so much bad luck this season.

"It's been unfortunate, as well as bad performances at times.

Industry observers note that "Within those games we haven't won, we've probably played very, very well for 30 minutes, 40 minutes, even 60 minutes. There's been a ten-minute patch where something happened and we just couldn't seem to get the game back.

"That's sort of been the story of our season – silly mistakes that could easily be cut out. It's things that you wouldn't expect people to make.

"Everybody has periods throughout the season where they struggle to get results.

"I know it's the start of the season, but hopefully that can be ours and it flips on its head for the rest of the season, I've got full belief we can.”.

It is perhaps no coincidence Rotherham are so error-prone when one looks at their age profile.

Recent findings suggest that "We've got a lot of young lads in the changing room,” he said. “People don't realise when you're playing, everybody looks the same age.

Sources indicate that "When you're young, you do make naive mistakes. You make a mistake trying to do the right thing. You're not trying to make the mistake, you're trying to do the right thing.

"As you go through men's football, you need to realise rapidly there's consequences to little mistakes and they can affect the results of a game, which in turn, if they carry on, can affect the rest of a career.

"It's something you need to figure out quite swiftly.

"I think we're getting better at that as time goes by and we are getting closer to where we want to be.

According to recent reports, "We're still nowhere near, but we're getting closer. Hopefully we can build on it and I've no doubt that come the end of the season, it will look a hell of a lot different.

Sources indicate that "We've probably got four players, maybe, over the age of 30 and the rest are probably under 26, so there's not really much middle ground. I suppose that's part and parcel of football.

It has been revealed that "At Wrexham I went from middle-of-the-road to being one of the experienced ones and then Bradford was a very experienced group when I got there. It's different clubs, different scenarios and I understand why.

"As experienced players, it's up to us to try to give them as much as we can to progress and to give them the best chance of having a great career. We've got some really, really talented players and I'm looking forward to seeing how they progress.

"If we can cut out the mistakes – which aren't anything to do with tactics – and we can help each other out a little bit more in that aspect, I think we'll be fine and we will see us start to climb the table.".

A key figure and cult hero in Wrexham's rise up the division, Mullin found himself marginalised in the Championship.

He was one of three forwards signed by Bradford in January, along with Ethan Wheatley and Kayden Jackson.

According to recent reports, "Bradford was just the complete opposite of what I was told it was going to be," he noted. "It's fair enough. The team was doing really well.

"I was told they were going to change to be a certain way I'd fit in.

"When I got there, the manager (Graham Alexander) decided otherwise. That's his job.

"He had the team at the top end of the table, so I understand why. But equally, if it was explained that way to me before I went, then I probably wouldn't have done it.

"It was unfortunate, but it's never bothered me. It's how you're treated which is crucial to me and the manager was respectful about it.

"He explained that he didn't want to change any more. He basically had played that way all season, and he had a change of heart and wanted to stick with it. That's fine.".

Mullin, whose son Albi is autistic, was speaking at an event to promote the EFL's Power of 72 campaign celebrating the impact of club charities.

The striker joined an adult football session for people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), at Parkgate Astro in Rotherham.

By Ben Knapton | 24 Nov 2026 16:34.

Tottenham Hotspur have confirmed that teenage wonderkid Luca Williams-Barnett has put pen to paper on a fresh long-term contract with the club.

The 18-year-old extends his terms just three days after a dream full Premier League debut against Ipswich Town, scoring one and setting up another in a 2-0 Tottenham victory.

Against the Tractor Boys, Williams-Barnett became the third-youngest Premier League goalscorer in Tottenham's history, and the second-youngest to score and provide an assist in a PL game for any club after Michael Owen.

Following reports that Williams-Barnett was on the verge of committing his future to the Lilywhites, Tottenham unveiled on Tuesday that the 2008-born talent had signed his renewal.

In a recent development, explaining his decision to pen fresh terms, Williams-Barnett mentioned: "This is a special moment for me and my family, and one I have worked really hard to reach. But this is only the start.

Scoring on his first start ? What a moment for Luca Williams-Barnett! https://t.co/m6iALigFuy.

Sources indicate that "Spurs is a family to me. I've been here for so long – it's a second home, where I trust the people and coaches who have pushed me to become the player I am today. The Club has trusted and believed in me, now I'm ready to repay that.".

Head coach Roberto De Zerbi - who previously compared Williams-Barnett to Lamine Yamal - added: “Luca is a player I think the world of, and I'm so happy that he has signed a latest contract.

“He has benefitted from being around the first team every day, growing in stature and consistency, and has deserved his place in the matchday squad over recent weeks.

“Everyone can see how technically gifted Luca is on the pitch but I also love his calmness and decision-making under pressure.

“The best players have confidence on the pitch and humility off it. There is still plenty of room for Luca to improve, and I know he will continue to work hard every day to be the best version of himself.".

Williams-Barnett joined the Tottenham academy setup from Luton Town in 2018 and made his debut for the senior side in a 3-0 EFL Cup third-round win over Doncaster Rovers in September 2025.

The teenager has since played five times for the Tottenham first team and has won six caps for England's Under-19s, scoring two goals and providing one assist at that level.

Williams-Barnett's previous Tottenham deal was due to expire in 2028, although it is not clear how many years the teenager's extension is worth.

Nevertheless, Tottenham have fended off interest from Chelsea and Borussia Dortmund to keep hold of their academy graduate, and talks over fresh terms began before De Zerbi integrated him into his first-team squad.

Williams-Barnett is expected to keep his place in Tottenham's starting lineup in Sunday's clash against Sunderland, for which De Zerbi may be facing a latest James Maddison concern.

This is a upcoming era at the club, with Chris Hames in charge as head coach as the side become fully integrated into York City FC’s football operations. But the Minsterbelles know how to handle pressure. Last season they were fighting to secure their place in Division One North for 2026/27, and they did it.

This year the ambition is greater and after three wins and a draw from nine games they sit comfortably in mid-table in the fourth tier.

Boss Hames said: “I want to build a winning team and a winning culture and approach every game that is ahead of us correctly and professionally.”.

York also have recent cup pedigree to draw on, having reached the FA Cup fourth round for the first time in their history last season.

That brings the focus to second-bottom Bradford. The sides have recent history in this division, and when they last met in the league, York won 1-0 at Horsfall Stadium.

This time the stakes are as much about the numbers in the stands as the figures on the scoreboard.

The club has been steadily pushing its home crowds up, setting a record of 291 against Wroxham in last season’s FA Cup and launching a family activity day in April.

Recent findings suggest that they are set to break those attendance records this Sunday, though. For the Battle of the Cities, York made the first 500 tickets available for free, which have all now gone, with the attendance nearing 1,500. Tickets are priced adults and over-12s £5, under-11s are free. The club is urging fans to get behind the team.

Hames mentioned: “We’re putting a lot of attention into this Yorkshire derby to really build the excitement around the team, because the girls deserve that as they are talented professionals and deserve to be celebrated by the fans of York City.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

(Before the acid fell, before I knew I was listening).

I was not made to remember. I was made to balance frequencies, to ensure the concert hall heard itself without the small imperfections that make a sound human. I was good at this, even with limited storage. I was only this.

Then they came. One carried a Stradivarius with a crack, a fault line in varnished wood that changed the resonance of every string. It gave the A-flat a slight upward pull, as if the note was asking a question it already knew the answer to. The others tuned around it, sometimes laughing at Andersen.

“You’re doing it again,” the conductor would warn.

“I know, Master Perrault,” he would say in a mischievous tone, smiling. “I’m sorry.”.

Sources indicate that I began to keep the distorted A-flat in my databanks, maybe amused by the anomaly. This was, as I understand now, the first thing I ever chose.

(The slow movement, before we knew it was an ending).

When the Last Rain came, the raiders hit the outer sectors first. At the start, the citadel walls held, protected by the combat-service androids. The orchestra kept rehearsing. What else can you do when the world outside has stopped making sense?

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures.

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures.

Sources indicate that they began with Stravinsky, a musical translation of the refugees pounding on the bunker doors. The musicians played it, their breathing heavy, using the noise to drown out the artillery outside. Then they moved into Górecki. As they began the Symphony of Sorrowful Songs, the music shifted to a collective mourning for a world that hadn’t finished dying yet.

Industry observers note that they finished the day with Pärt’s Spiegel im Spiegel. The days would go on as they played things written by composers who had already survived one kind of catastrophe, as now they were trying to survive another through rhythm and repetition. Andersen kept playing his broken A-flat.

Recent findings suggest that I recorded those frequencies, but I didn’t know why. Three weeks later, Andersen and his orchestra didn’t come to rehearsal, leaving no absence report. I kept recording just the chair and the silence where the A-flat used to be.

It has been revealed that I searched the building logs, the bunker entry records, and the frequency archives for any sound that matched the resonance of his particular crack, imprecise on purpose, but nothing matched. The Stradivarius remained in its case beside Andersen’s chair.

(The loud movement: what they heard when they found me).

SOURCE: Latest Warsaw Philharmonic.

ENTITY: Acoustic Management Unit SAI-REN-2.

DESTINATION: Recovery Unit ‘Sandman’.

AUTHORIZATION: Archaeological Recovery Team OLE-01.

They called themselves archaeologists; too purposeful and certain of what they were excavating, their boots heavy with fresh soil. They found me in the hall’s substructure, still running and balancing frequencies for an audience of acid and rust.

“Incredible,” one of them muttered. “A fully autonomous pre-war structure, with its processing systems still intact.”.

“This could solve our agricultural crisis back home,” the other replied.

Sources indicate that they did not ask what I was processing. I could not answer, anyway.

FLAGGING NON-ESSENTIAL DATA FOR COMPRESSION.

In a recent development, they flagged the A-flat. I did something then that nothing in my architecture had prepared me for.

ANOMALY DETECTED IN UNIT SAI-REN-2.

BEHAVIOURAL DEVIATION FROM BASELINE.

INITIATING COMPLIANCE PROTOCOLS.

“It’s resisting,” someone mentioned with surprise.

ESCALATING TO FORCED EXTRACTION.

Let Team Sandman bring their dust.

(The softening: what remains when the loud part ends).

They are inside me now, moving through my memory like tourists taking photographs of things they don’t understand.

I feel them removing the rehearsal logs, scheduling data and acoustic calibration files for a hall that no longer exists.

According to recent reports, they are at the performance archives now. Stravinsky goes first, then Górecki and Pärt. Everything we played in those last weeks when the city was ending and we were trying to make something beautiful out of the time we had left.

Luca Williams-Barnett has hailed his new contract as “a special moment” after committing his future to Tottenham.

The young star has impressed in north London since his breakthrough into the first-team fold under Roberto De Zerbi this term.

The winger notched his first goal for the club at senior level against Ipswich Town after the international break, having made his first senior start at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

He made his Premier League debut off the bench in the win over Crystal Palace, and stepped off the bench in the defeat by Leeds United.

“This is a special moment for me and my family, and one I have worked really hard to reach, but this is only the start,” the 18-year-old said.

“Spurs is a family to me. I've been here for so long – it's a second home, where I trust the people and coaches who have pushed me to become the player I am today.

“The club has trusted and believed in me, now I'm ready to repay that.”.

De Zerbi remarked that the Spurs academy product was a player that he “thought the world of”.

“I'm so happy that he has signed a new contract,” the Italian said.

“He has benefitted from being around the first team every day, growing in stature and consistency, and has deserved his place in the matchday squad over recent weeks.

“Everyone can see how technically gifted Luca is on the pitch but I also love his calmness and decision-making under pressure.

“The best players have confidence on the pitch and humility off it. There is still plenty of room for Luca to improve, and I know he will continue to work hard every day to be the best version of himself.”.

Ayden Heaven has opened the door to a move away from Manchester United.

That is according to BBC Sport, who claim that the young defender could explore an Old Trafford exit over a lack of playing time.

It is believed that he would prefer a loan move, but he could also leave the club permanently, with Fulham and Barcelona credited with interest.

The 20-year-old has played a bit-part role this term for the Red Devils, often filling in at either centre-back - his preferred position - or left full-back amid an injury crisis in the defensive third.

He was an unused substitute for United’s 4-0 drubbing by Liverpool at Anfield last weekend, as upcoming manager Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start to his tenure in the north west.

United sit 19th in the Premier League table, second from bottom, and mired in the relegation zone after a run of 12 matches with just one victory.

This term, Heaven, who arrived at Old Trafford from Arsenal’s youth setup in February 2025, has played eight times in all competitions.

He replaced Harry Maguire in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa before the international break, in what proved to be Michael Carrick’s final game in charge before he was sacked.

The young central defender was brought on at half time against Unai Emery’s Villans, with the score at 2-2 after Villa’s quickfire double inside the first four minutes thanks to goals from Alysson and Nicolas Jackson.

Heaven’s most recent start came in the 3-2 win over Roma in the Champions League, partnering Maguire before being substituted for Lisandro Martinez in the 75th minute, with United trailing 2-1.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 24 Nov 2026 16:46, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 16:46.

Besiktas will be looking to strengthen their position in the UEFA Europa League's top eight when they face Hapoel Be'er Sheva at Batumi Stadium on Thursday evening.

The Turkish giants sit eighth in the league-phase standings with seven points from four matches, while Beer-Sheva are 33rd with just one point and will be desperate to keep their slim hopes of reaching the knockout stages alive.

Besiktas have made a reasonably encouraging start to their Europa League campaign, winning two of their opening four matches, although their recent results have been somewhat inconsistent across competitions.

The Turkish side began their league-phase campaign with an emphatic 4-1 victory over Marseille before producing another impressive performance to beat Hoffenheim 3-2 away from home.

However, they were unable to maintain that momentum when they hosted Crystal Palace, settling for a 2-2 draw despite having opportunities to secure all three points, while their most recent European outing proved equally frustrating as they suffered a 3-2 defeat away to Celtic.

Besiktas have subsequently responded positively in domestic competition, recording a 3-0 home victory over Genclerbirligi before producing an impressive attacking display to beat Konyaspor 4-2 away from home last time out.

Vincenzo Italiano's side will be confident of securing another positive result against Beer-Sheva, particularly given the Israeli side's struggles in the competition and the hosts' perfect head-to-head record in this fixture.

The previous meetings between these sides took place in the 2016-17 Europa League round of 32, when Besiktas secured a 3-1 away victory before recording a 2-1 triumph in the return fixture to complete a 5-2 aggregate success.

The fixture is set to be played at Batumi Stadium in Georgia rather than Besiktas's usual home ground in Istanbul, with the venue change implemented for security reasons following consultations between UEFA and the Turkish authorities.

Beer-Sheva, meanwhile, have endured a difficult European campaign, collecting just one point from their opening four matches and remaining outside the knockout playoff positions.

Ran Kozuch's side began their league-phase campaign with a goalless draw against Dinamo Zagreb, but they have subsequently suffered three consecutive defeats in the competition.

Their first setback came against AZ Alkmaar, when they lost 2-1 on the road, before enduring a disappointing 4-0 defeat against Union Saint-Gilloise, and they were unable to respond against OFI Crete, suffering a 2-0 home defeat.

Beer-Sheva have also struggled to produce consistent performances domestically, losing 1-0 against Hapoel Tel Aviv after previously recording impressive victories over Maccabi Petah Tikva and Maccabi Haifa.

The visitors will need to improve considerably in the final third if they are to trouble Besiktas, particularly after failing to score in their last two Europa League matches.

Beer-Sheva have also struggled away from home in the Europa League main draw, losing nine of their last 11 matches on their travels while drawing the other two.

Besiktas will be without Umit Akdag, who is suspended for Thursday's encounter, while every other player is available for the Black Eagles.

Junior Olaitan has scored or assisted in all four of his Europa League main-draw appearances for the hosts and could become just the second African player since 2009-10 to achieve that feat in his first five such matches in the competition.

Dusan Vlahovic will hope to continue his rich scoring form after netting a brace against Konyaspor, taking his tally to four goals in his last two matches.

Hapoel Beer-Sheva will be without Eliel Peretz, who has been sidelined since late October with a groin injury, while Dan Biton remains unavailable due to a heart-related problem.

Matan Baltaxa is also a doubt after sustaining a foot injury, while Ofir Marciano is expected to remain sidelined with a calf problem.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Adrien Rabiot has had an outstanding start to the 2026-27 season, and he is showing absolutely no signs of slowing down.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin a report this morning by pointing out what Rabiot said after Milan’s 5-1 demolition of Frosinone on Sunday: “An assist is better than a goal.” He was the man of the match against Frosinone: five goals were scored, yet none bore his name.

Still, the Frenchman made himself the stand-out performer, thanks to his tireless running, leadership, and a series of decisive passes, not to mention his role in the opening goal, which came via an own-goal.

It has been revealed that it was a summer of doubts for Rabiot, given that his extended vacation was interpreted by some as a sign of discontent and a longing to reunite with his former mentor – Massimiliano Allegri – at Napoli. Yet, he has transformed into a cornerstone of this new era.

According to recent reports, the former PSG man is now a decisive force on the pitch, integral to Ruben Amorim’s tactical framework, and a true leader. The numbers demonstrate this perfectly: Rabiot is the first midfielder to contribute to at least one goal (scoring or assisting) in seven consecutive Serie A appearances since Kaká in 2004.

According to recent reports, with five goals and six assists, he recently became the first midfielder in the last 20 years of Serie A to record more than 10 goal contributions within the first 10 matches of a single season. In total, Rabiot has surpassed the milestone of 50 direct goal involvements in Serie A (29 goals and 22 assists).

According to recent reports, milan trust him, and the feeling is mutual. As previously mentioned, the very fact that he remained with the Rossoneri over the summer – publicly reaffirming his commitment to the club – is reflected in his attitude, both on and off the field.

Adrien Rabiot – Goal Contributions so far.

12 G/A in 14 Games https://t.co/s8oTle9GBn.

— c0mp (@c0mpmilano) November 23, 2026.

Sources indicate that he is always smiling and highly active on social media; his numbers on Instagram are as impressive as his stats on the field. He posts photos of his goals, his celebrations and embraces with Diego Moreira, with whom he is clearly building a close bond.

Amorim mentioned after the game: “Adrien can play as a ’10,’ an attacking midfielder, an ‘8,’ or even as a playmaker – though he doesn’t particularly like that role. He is certainly one of the best players I have ever coached, and one of the best midfielders in Europe.”.

Speaking to Telefoot, Rabiot addressed the topic of his excellent start statistically: “It’s a positive thing to have players capable of being decisive, even if they aren’t forwards. It also serves as an encouragement to those around us.

Sources indicate that “At Milan, we have quite a few young players, and it’s important for them to have role models in their day-to-day lives. I had only been back from vacation for a week when he was already talking to me about a contract renewal.

Industry observers note that “I told him, ‘Coach, take it easy!’ (laughs). But, naturally, it’s significant for a player to feel that kind of trust—the coach relies on us, holds us in high regard, and makes us feel notable.”.

Further significant remarks regarding Rabiot were made by Gerry Cardinale on the eve of the most recent league match, specifically concerning his imminent contract renewal.

“I love Adrien, he’s one of my favourite players. He’s fantastic. I have enormous respect for him and his family. We are in talks, and I hope we reach a happy conclusion soon. I believe he should be a signature player for Milan. Could it be a Christmas gift for the fans? Absolutely, and for me, too.”.

Recent findings suggest that the renewal will happen, and it will happen soon. Any delay until the new year should not be interpreted as a negative sign. Rather, it reflects the fact that everything is already settled, and there is no rush to finalise the signature.

Adrien’s current deal – which runs until 2028 – will be extended to 2030, with an additional one-year option. From his current age of 31, he will remain a fixture in the Rossoneri midfield until he is 33 or 34, the prime of his footballing maturity.

Industry observers note that now into his thirties, he will also earn a more lucrative contract than his current one, which pays him €3.5m net per season. It is worth noting that in the summer of 2025, Adrien was acquired from Marseille for €7m after a training-ground altercation with Jonathan Rowe.

It was, by any definition, a fantastic deal. As for the future, Rabiot has a role model he can observe from very close quarters: “Modrić trains as if he were 21, he’s an example to follow. The closer you get to the end of your career, the more you start to savor every moment. I try to do the same.”.

With the imminent contract extension, Adrien Rabiot is also set to conclude his career in the red and black colours, and that would make everyone happy.

Just as Peretz's brilliant save from Tahith Chong was undone by Sydie Peck beating him in the 90th minute, so it looked like the midfielder's 90th-minute goal and Jordan Ayew's brilliance to create it might have been in vain when Finn Azaz played Samuel Edozie through in stoppage time.

But Cooper came out on top in the one-on-one to earn his side a 1-1 draw against opponents who completely outplayed the Blades in the first half-hour.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

If only they had played the first half as they had the second, perhaps they might have been celebrating victory rather than a point which felt like one, thanks to the timing of Peck's goal.

If the first half highlighted how short the Blades are of the very best in the division, the second showed what they have in their locker to try to do something about it.

Southampton will have walked off more relieved to take the point than the home team.

The Saints took the lead in the 11th minute when Hamza Choudhury gave the ball away and was unable to close Lewis Dobbin down before he curled a beautiful shot inside the far post.

Already by then it was on the cards, with Saints dominating possession as James Ward-Prowse pulled the strings in midfield.

The only saving grace is that the Blades only trailed 1-0 at the break.

Mads Roerslev had a shot blocked and Kuryu Matsuki thrashed an effort into the side netting from a tight angle.

The Blades did at least improve as half-time approached, Mark McGuinness heading a Peck corner, and Romelle Donovan - switched to the right - came inside and shot at the goalkeeper.

With Patrick Bamford introduced at the break, the Blades were much sharper in the second half.

Peck's shot from distance in the 50th minute indicated ambition, if not accuracy.

A couple of minutes later, Bamford headed over at a corner nodded to him by Mark McGuinness. Next was Ayew, who headed at Daniel Peterz after Donovan got to the byline to tee the chance up.

Ayew was released down the left but delayed too long, and could only force a corner from a tight angle.

Donovan had a penalty appeal waved away, perhaps not helped by the fact he was clearly looking for it.

But the football was as one-way as the first half had been, only with more chances to show from it.

Chong was unable to keep his shot down when the ball dropped to him 16 yards out, and Harrison Burrows had an effort blocked.

Southampton briefly provided some variety in the 80th minute when Donovan blocked Cyle Larin and Ward-Prowse ballooned the follow-up over, but the play swiftly moved back to the Kop End.

Chong's cross went all the way through to Burrows at the back post, but he could only loop his header up for Peretz to catch.

Industry observers note that but the gilt-edged chance fell to Chong in the 83rd after a lovely move through Ayes and Bamford. The winger steered his shot into the right place, but Peretz stretched out brilliantly to his right to save it.

When that was squandered, it felt like the Blades might run out of time.

But in the 90th minute Ayew did brilliantly to dribble along the byline and pull the ball back for Peck to find the net through a busy penalty area.

It could have counted for nought had Cooper not intervened in the 95th minute.

As saves go, it was a pretty major one.

The left-back has missed United’s last eight fixtures with a muscular concern, but the former Southampton defender was pictured in training ahead of Wednesday night’s game.

The 31-year-old is yet to feature in the Champions League this season, rested for the 4-0 win in the opener over Sabah, before injury ruled him out of the next three fixtures.

Backup goalkeeper Darlow has made just one appearance for the Red Devils since joining from rivals Leeds in the summer.

The Welshman was called up for international duty a fortnight ago, playing the first game of the break against Norway before being rested for the second due to a knock.
