💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Adepoju Marvellous | 24 Nov 2026 16:54, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 20:35.
  • Ajax and Thun face off at the Johan Cruyff Arena on Thursday as the 2026-27 Conference League campaign reaches its midway point.
  • Both teams emerged victorious in their last continental outings and now look to build on that momentum on the European stage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adepoju Marvellous | 24 Nov 2026 16:54, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 20:35.

Ajax and Thun face off at the Johan Cruyff Arena on Thursday as the 2026-27 Conference League campaign reaches its midway point.

Both teams emerged victorious in their last continental outings and now look to build on that momentum on the European stage.

Returning to action after agonisingly surrendering a two-goal lead to FC Twente before the international break, Ajax made light work of Eredivisie newcomers ADO Den Haag, cruising to a 3-0 victory on Sunday thanks to two goals from Davy Klaassen and a strike from Jorthy Mokio.

Michel’s side have now claimed six victories from their last seven matches in all competitions since losing to Hajduk Split in their Conference League opener in mid-October, with subsequent continental outings yielding wins over Atalanta and Midtjylland by a combined score of 8-1.

Central to De Godenzonen’s resurgence has been their ability to start promptly, with Klaassen's opener last time out marking the seventh consecutive match in which they have broken the deadlock.

Ajax currently sit outside the guaranteed knockout places in the Conference League and will be keen to collect maximum points to break into the top eight, thereby avoiding the additional hurdle of a playoff tie in an already congested campaign.

Thursday’s game marks the third meeting between the sides, with the hosts seeking to maintain their perfect record in this fixture, having come out on top in both group-stage encounters of the 2005-06 Champions League en route to a last-16 exit.

Thun ended a 13-year absence from European competition by qualifying for this season’s Conference League, but a pair of 1-0 defeats in their opening two matches against FC Twente and Hajduk Split meant their return to continental action began on a sour note.

Days after netting four times in the final 20 minutes of a nine-goal thriller against Lausanne-Sport to claim a remarkable triumph, Gian-Luca Privitelli starred against Scottish outfit Hearts, leading Thun to a 3-1 victory to finally get their European campaign up and running at the third attempt.

Back-to-back winless games against Basel and Young Boys have followed, so Die Oberlander head to Amsterdam with confidence low and knowing that a defeat could see them drop out of the knockout playoff places, so there is little margin for error.

Recent findings suggest that thun have conceded in each of their last 13 competitive matches, including 11 goals in their most recent four. Tightening up defensively will be essential if the Swiss side are to end their ongoing three-game losing run against Dutch opponents.

  • The Dutchman has missed each of the Reds' last three games with a heel fracture and was unsurprisingly not included in Liverpool's 22-man squad for the trip to the Jan Breydel Stadion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 24 Nov 2026 17:13, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 17:13.

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has dropped a worrying admission over Ryan Gravenberch's fitness ahead of Wednesday's Champions League clash with Club Brugge.

The Dutchman has missed each of the Reds' last three games with a heel fracture and was unsurprisingly not included in Liverpool's 22-man squad for the trip to the Jan Breydel Stadion.

Gravenberch had returned to training before Liverpool's 4-0 win over Manchester United in Sunday's Premier League affair, but the former Ajax man is still no closer to a competitive comeback.

After landing in Belgium, Iraola fielded questions from the media in his pre-game press conference, and he admitted that Gravenberch's injury was proving more complex to solve than initially anticipated.

Sources indicate that "With Ryan, it's a bit more difficult," Iraola mentioned. "He's having pain, the things in the fascia are difficult to solve. Sometimes he's managing the pain, but now he's not in a good place. Let's see if we can find ways to solve the problem but they are injuries that are not easy to solve normally.".

While the exact nature and severity of Gravenberch's injury is not entirely clear, the Netherlands international may be suffering from Plantar fasciitis, which would fit Iraola's description.

An inflammation of the heel, Plantar fasciitis can take anywhere between four and 12 weeks to get better, and Gravenberch has already been out since the beginning of November.

As a result, the Dutchman may be missing until the end of January in the worst-case scenario, meaning he would firstly miss matches against Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur, Porto and Aston Villa before the end of the year.

Liverpool then face Manchester United, Inter Milan and Everton again in the early weeks of 2027, and it remains to be seen if Gravenberch's complex problem has settled down by then.

The 24-year-old has set up one goal in 12 appearances for Liverpool so far this season, and in his absence, Alexis Mac Allister, Trey Nyoni, Dominik Szoboszlai and James McConnell will be competing for midfield minutes.

As well as delivering a negative patch on Gravenberch, Iraola also revealed that Cody Gakpo would likely miss the weekend's Merseyside derby with Everton too.

The attacker hurt his calf while representing the Netherlands during the international break, although Iraola has insisted that his issue is not severe.

Recent findings suggest that "With Cody, it's a soleus injury," Iraola added. "It's not significant but we expect he'll be out for the weekend. But it's more predictable.".

Giovanni Leoni (knee), Conor Bradley (knee) and Hugo Ekitike (Achilles) are also on the sidelines for Liverpool, who sit eighth in the Champions League league-phase table with nine points from their opening four fixtures.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Improvements in education, lifestyle and health during early life are slowing rates of cognitive decline in older people.Credit: Laura Olivas/Getty.

Recent findings suggest that people entering their golden years now have better memory and experience slower cognitive decline than previous generations. A study of people born between 1910 and 1964 found that a ten-year jump in birth date was associated with a 10% higher memory score at the age of 60. Researchers speculate that improvements in memory might be thanks to better education, health care and nutrition in childhood, while the slower decline in cognitive function might be influenced by factors later in life, such as improved treatment for cardiovascular and metabolic disease.

Reference: Nature Medicine paper.

Recent findings suggest that the large language models that underlie chatbots such as ChatGPT are promptly overcoming some of their weaknesses, say computer scientists Owen Queen and James Zou. They analysed flaws — such as hallucinating references — that had been flagged by researchers in academic papers. Most flaws were no longer a problem within roughly 16 months of a paper’s publication — for example, the latest models hardly ever attribute information to sources that don’t exist. On the other hand, newer models are getting more sycophantic and worse at generating random numbers.

Reference: Owen Queen & James Zou blog post.

Sources indicate that undergraduate students were consistently the first group to start spreading emerging variants of the SARS-CoV-2 virus between 2021 and 2023, according to a massive genetic analysis. Researchers found that viral transmission during that period was highest among school students between the ages of 15 and 18, university undergrads and nursing-home residents. However, staff at all three types of institution had about the same risk of contracting COVID-19 as did those in their surrounding communities. The study’s scale “is truly impressive”, claims infectious-disease researcher Bill Hanage.

According to recent reports, A report by the US National Academies of Sciences, Engineering and Medicine (NASEM) suggests that science publishers take too long to retract or correct research papers, and standards for doing so are applied inconsistently across journals. NASEM recommends that the editorial review process be completed within 12 weeks for most cases and should rarely stretch beyond 6 months. The report was due to be published on 19 November, but was delayed after journalists at Science noted that it contained references with fabricated author names, which could suggest that artificial intelligence was used to draft or edit it.

Sources indicate that earlier this week we tried our hands at a game that tests our ability to decode ‘tortured phrases’ — ridiculous synonyms for common terms, which are intended to obscure plagiarism. For example, instead of ‘major data’, a study might use ‘colossal information’. The quiz inspired Briefing reader Chris Schneider to suggest her own tongue-in-cheek tortured phrase for our own dear ‘Nature Briefing’: “Essence of donning underwear.”.

In the spirit of silliness, we’d like to hear your best science-related tortured phrases — whether spotted in the wild or invented just for fun. Entertain us at briefing@nature.com.

Bees are the well-deserved superstars of the pollination world, and the reputations of birds, bats and even wasps are on the rise. Make room, now, for flies. Diptera — especially hoverflies (Syrphidae) — are undervalued pollinators. For example, on strawberry farms in England, hoverflies can make up more than half of the pollinating insects. Meanwhile, our reliance on managed honeybees can actually damage biodiversity and crop quality.

Now they wait to learn what comes next. The companion star could cause the giant star to shed its gas envelope, after which the two could settle into a tight orbit; or it could plunge into the giant star’s core to its doom. “To conclusively rule out either case, we need to continue observing the system,” indicates astrophysicist Viraj Karambelkar.

Manchester United have been boosted by the return of Luke Shaw for Wednesday's Champions League clash with Portuguese giants Sporting Lisbon.

Shaw has not featured for Man United since October 10 due to a muscular problem, but he returned to training ahead of the European match and has been named in the travelling squad.

The Englishman's return is major news for the Red Devils given their defensive problems, but it remains to be seen whether he is considered for a start on Wednesday.

Matheus Cunha is a notable absentee through suspension, with the Brazil international sent off in the team's last match in the competition against Roma.

Meanwhile, Carlos Baleba, Marcus Rashford and Benjamin Sesko remain sidelined alongside long-term absentee Manuel Ugarte.

Man United have six points to show from their four matches in the competition, which has left them in 18th in the overall table.

Head coach Mauricio Pochettino has major decisions to make when it comes to his defensive unit for this match, as Matthijs de Ligt struggled in the 4-0 loss to Liverpool last time out.

Leny Yoro had been facing a Premier League suspension, increasing his chances of being involved from the first whistle against Sporting.

However, Yoro's red card against Liverpool has been overturned following a successful appeal.

The 21-year-old will therefore now be available to face Brentford at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Karl Darlow has also returned to the squad for the Sporting trip, having recovered from the injury that forced him to miss out against Liverpool.

Goalkeepers: Senne Lammens, Karl Darlow, Tom Heaton.

Defenders: Harry Amass, Diogo Dalot, Matthijs de Ligt, Patrick Dorgu, Ayden Heaven, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez, Noussair Mazraoui, Luke Shaw, Leny Yoro.

Midfielders: Andrey Santos, Bruno Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo, Mason Mount, Youri Tielemans.

Forwards: Amad, Shea Lacey, Bryan Mbeumo, Joshua Zirkzee.

Manchester United will have Leny Yoro available for Saturday's Premier League clash against Brentford, with his one-game suspension being removed.

Yoro was sent off in the early stages of Sunday's Premier League clash with Liverpool following a last-man challenge on Reds forward Alexander Isak.

The France international was facing a one-game suspension, ruling him out of Man United's next Premier League fixture against Brentford.

However, the ban has now been removed following a successful appeal.

"Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal," read a statement from the Football Association.

Recent findings suggest that "The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November. The independent Regulatory Commission’s written reasons for its decision will be published in due course.".

There had been a lot of debate surrounding whether the foul was a clear denial of a goalscoring opportunity, as Isak appeared to lose possession of the ball.

Breaking: Leny Yoro's red card against Liverpool has been overturned.? https://t.co/GIdwIWXdUs.

Man United head coach Mauricio Pochettino and midfielder Kobbie Mainoo both criticised the decision in their post-match comments.

"The ball was for the goalkeeper. In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, [Yoro] never had the intention to connect with Isak," said Pochettino.

"When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper.".

Mainoo, meanwhile, stated: "The game's been taken out of our hands by a red card that I don't think can be a red card. No chance. The ball's already with the goalkeeper.".

Yoro is at the moment with the Man United squad in Portugal preparing for Wednesday's Champions League fixture with Sporting Lisbon.

Arsenal dropped points from a winning position for the second time in as many games following a 1-1 Champions League draw with Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium.

Mikel Arteta’s men led at the interval after Viktor Gyokeres scored his first goal on home soil in 206 days with a wonderful 25-yard opener inside 10 minutes.

READ MATT VERRI’S ANALYSIS HERE!

But just as they did in the Premier League at Newcastle on Saturday, Arsenal were unable to see out the victory, with Maximilian Beier netting for the visitors after half-time.

Jobe Bellingham had a goal ruled out for offside, while Gyokeres could perhaps count himself fortunate not to give away a penalty when a Dortmund corner struck him on the arm.

Gyokeres then wasted a golden opportunity to restore Arsenal’s advantage when he headed wide unmarked from six yards, while the ball cannoned off Serhou Guirassy to twice strike the Dortmund post in the closing stages. Declan Rice hit the woodwork again for Arsenal with five minutes left.

The draw leaves Arsenal fifth in the table, but they could be on the bubble of the top-eight places – which are assured of automatic qualification for the next phase – if results work against them on Wednesday.

Gyokeres was introduced only as a stoppage-time substitute in Arsenal’s 2-2 draw at St James’ Park despite the Gunners chasing the game for most of the second half.

Here, he began from the start and opened the scoring with his first meaningful contribution of the game.

Noni Madueke had time and space to bring down a crossfield ball before finding Gyokeres, who immediately tried his luck from range, and perhaps catching Gregor Kobel in the visiting goal by surprise.

But that was to take away nothing from the velocity and dip behind Gyokeres’ effort – the sort of strike which encouraged Arsenal to spend £68million last summer but has not always been repaid. It was Gyokeres’ first at the Emirates since May.

Rice fired over from range and then only a last-ditch tackle from Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck denied the England midfielder moments later. Arsenal led at the break, but they did in the North East before a second-half collapse saw them emerge with just a point, rather than three.

Beier afforded Arsenal a warning almost immediately after the interval when he ghosted to the front post only to fail to get any sort of connection on Daniel Svensson’s low cross.

But Beier made no mistake in the 55th minute. Joane Gadou was the architect following a fine run from inside his own half. He looked up to find Beier, who took one touch past Gabriel before unleashing a low drive. Kepa Arrizabalaga, deputising for the injured David Raya, never got close to saving it.

It has been revealed that piero Hincapie’s header was saved by Kobel as Arsenal mustered a response. Bellingham thought he had put Dortmund ahead when he turned away Kepa’s bungled save but the assistant referee’s offside flag came to Arsenal’s rescue.

Then came the Arsenal onslaught. Madueke’s curling shot grazed the side-netting before Gyokeres sent a diving header wide from six yards to leave Arteta on his knees. Arsenal also struck a post on three occasions.

Recent findings suggest that in all, the Gunners had 29 shots but only four of those were on target, and the need for a world-class finisher remains a top priority should Arsenal want to win the Champions League for the first time in their history. They will face Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid next.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Merseyside Police reportedly arrested seven supporters at last weekend's clash between Manchester United and Liverpool, with two on suspicion of tragedy chanting.
  • The bitter rivals met at Anfield for the first time in the Premier League season as Mauricio Pochettino kicked off his stint as Man United manager - under the most concerning circumstances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 03:43 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 03:45 EST, 24 November 2026.

Merseyside Police reportedly arrested seven supporters at last weekend's clash between Manchester United and Liverpool, with two on suspicion of tragedy chanting.

The bitter rivals met at Anfield for the first time in the Premier League season as Mauricio Pochettino kicked off his stint as Man United manager - under the most concerning circumstances.

But even before the visitors saw Leny Yoro sent off and four conceded without reply, this fixture has long been one of the most incendiary in the top flight.

Supporters arrested for suspected tragedy chanting are thought to be a 63-year-old man from Heywood, Greater Manchester, and a 57-year-old man from Wallasey, in Wirral, as per the Athletic.

Both clubs have waged independent battles against tragedy chanting, which sees fans taunt opponents by mocking major disasters, such as Hillsborough, the Heysel Stadium disaster, and the Munich air disaster.

Some tragedy chants are even aimed at the personal lives of players on the pitch, and in 2024, fresh guidance from the Crown Prosecution saw tragedy chanting upgraded to a criminal offence.

Seven people have been arrested following Man United's trip to face Liverpool at Anfield (police pictured breaking up a fight in the away end).

As well as tragedy chanting, a 47-year-old man from Swinton, Greater Manchester, was arrested on suspicion of possession of a class A drug.

Two men - a 49-year-old from Didsbury, South Manchester, and a 38-year-old from Denton, Greater Manchester - were arrested on suspicion of indecent and racialist chanting.

A further two, aged 30 and 23, were arrested during the final minutes of Sunday's clash as a skirmish broke out among the away supporters at Anfield.

But despite the enmity between the two teams, there were a greater number of arrests last month, when Man City visited Anfield for the first match in the wake of the revelation that the club had been found guilty of the vast majority of charges levelled at them for breaching the Premier League's financial regulations between 2009 and 2018.

That fixture saw 10 fans arrested, with five arrested on suspicion of tragedy chanting.

The match-up between the two sides became increasingly charged with the establishment of a rivalry at the top of the table under former managers Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola.

In 2018, the Man City bus was attacked with bottles, bricks and flares ahead of a Champions League meeting between the two sides, with future fixtures in Liverpool at times seeing the players' bus route amended to avoid throngs of home fans.

In March 2025, Merseyside police requested an unorthodox kick-off of 3.45pm for the match, rather than the customary Sunday start time of 4.30pm, in a bid to reduce problems between the two sets of fans.

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 18:54, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 19:11.

Enzo Maresca has made a total of five changes to his Manchester City starting lineup for tonight’s Champions League clash against Napoli at the Etihad Stadium.

Matheus Nunes has recovered from an ankle injury and is fit to start, while Enzo Fernandez, Rayan Cherki, Josko Gvardiol and Allan also come into the side following last weekend’s 1-1 Premier League draw with Fulham.

Ruben Dias, Abdukodir Khusanov, Phil Foden, Iliman Ndiaye and Jeremy Doku all revert to the substitutes' bench for the visit of the Serie A side.

While Nunes will begin at right-back, Gvardiol is set to start at centre-back alongside Marc Guehi, with Nico O'Reilly retaining his spot at left-back.

Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi will continue to link arms in centre-midfield, with Fernandez expected to operate further forward in an advanced central role behind striker and captain Erling Haaland.

This could therefore see playmaker Rayan Cherki move out wide, with the Frenchman potentially occupying the left flank as Allan most likely begins on the right.

As for Napoli, head coach Massimiliano Allegri has made a total of three changes to the side that began the 1-0 win over Torino 04 in Serie A last weekend.

Kevin De Bruyne has been recalled to start against his former club for the second time since leaving in 2025. The legendary Belgian playmaker was sacrificed just 21 minutes into his first Etihad homecoming last season, following an early red card for captain Matteo Politano in a 2-0 defeat.

Defender Mathias Olivera and forward Noa Lang have also returned to Napoli’s first XI, with Rafa Marin, Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa and Antonio Vergara all making way.

Scotland duo Billy Gilmour and Scott McTominay – who scored the match-winner against Torino – will both start in centre-midfield, while ex-Man United striker Rasmus Hojlund will be supported by Lang in attack.

Manchester City starting lineup: Donnarumma; Nunes, Guehi, Gvardiol, O’Reilly; Bouaddi, Anderson; Allan, Fernandez, Cherki; Haaland.

Subs: Rulli, Dias, Ndiaye, Kovacic, Doku, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Khusanov, Foden, McAidoo, F. Samba, Lewis.

Napoli starting lineup: Milinkovic-Savic; Beukema, Rrahmani, Olivera; Politano, Gilmour, McTominay, De Bruyne, Spinazzola; Lang, Hojlund.

Subs: Contini, Spinielli, Neres, Lucca, Giovane, Chiumarriello, Anguissa.

Jude Bellingham insisted he does not "care about the Ballon d'Or" and would rather "win a lot of titles" with Real Madrid instead.

The England international stole the headlines in Madrid's 5-1 win over PSV in the Champions League on Tuesday after scoring a stunning goal.

Bellingham came on at half-time, with Los Blancos a goal down, and netted a sensational volley before also assisting Vinicius Junior late on at Estadio Bernabeu.

No side has won more Champions League games having been trailing at the break than Madrid, with this their 13th such victory (level with Barcelona).

Bellingham created three chances in the second half, won three of his four duels and recorded the joint-most final third entries (seven).

He finished 11th at this year's Ballon d'Or, but the 23-year-old is not focused on individual awards.

"I don't care about the Ballon d'Or, honestly," said Bellingham.

"I want to win a lot of titles with the team, the Champions League, the league.

"The Ballon d'Or is something for you, journalists, to vote and create a bit of tension. But for me it's more vital that the team win.".

Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund LIVE.

Arsenal dropped points from a winning position for the second time in as many games following a 1-1 Champions League draw with Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium.Mikel Arteta’s men led at the interval after Viktor Gyokeres scored his first goal on home soil in 206 days with a wonderful 25-yard opener inside 10 minutes.

But just as they did in the Premier League at Newcastle on Saturday, Arsenal were unable to see out the victory, with Maximilian Beier netting for the visitors after half-time. Jobe Bellingham had a goal ruled out for offside, while Gyokeres could perhaps count himself fortunate not to give away a penalty when a Dortmund corner struck him on the arm.

Gyokeres then wasted a golden opportunity to restore Arsenal’s advantage when he headed wide unmarked from six yards, while the ball cannoned off Serhou Guirassy to twice strike the Dortmund post in the closing stages. Declan Rice hit the woodwork again for Arsenal with five minutes left.

Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund latest updates.

Here was Arsenal’s very own Groundhog Day. Again.

Mikel Arteta would have feared what was coming as the misses piled up and his team found increasingly remarkable ways to not score.

Recent findings suggest that it was rinse and repeat from an Arsenal perspective. Completely dominate the opening 45 minutes with some sublime football. Take the lead but then fail to kick on. Drop the intensity in the second half and regret those missed opportunities.

How did Matt Verri rate the Arsenal players?

There we have it. Arsenal are held, the spoils are shared.

Thanks for joining us, be sure to come back very soon for even more live action.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 19:00, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 21:37.
  • Sunderland resume their Europa League campaign on Thursday night with a matchday five fixture against Polish outfit Jagiellonia Bialystok at the Stadium of Light.
  • While the Black Cats currently occupy 11th place in the 36-team League Phase standings, Jaga find themselves down in 27th place at the halfway stage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 19:00, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 21:37.

Sunderland resume their Europa League campaign on Thursday night with a matchday five fixture against Polish outfit Jagiellonia Bialystok at the Stadium of Light.

While the Black Cats currently occupy 11th place in the 36-team League Phase standings, Jaga find themselves down in 27th place at the halfway stage.

Sunderland’s first major European campaign in 53 years began with back-to-back victories over AZ Alkmaar (1-0) and Torreense (2-1), but they have since suffered setbacks against Lech Poznan and Dinamo Zagreb.

Regis Le Bris’s men were held to a 1-1 draw in Poland by Poznan on matchday three before, they were booed off by the Stadium of Light faithful following a disappointing 2-0 home defeat three weeks ago, seeing them slip out of the automatic last-16 qualification spots.

Since then, Sunderland supporters have had a lot more to be optimistic about, with four points collected and two clean sheets kept in Premier League matches against Chelsea and Aston Villa, beating the former at home 1-0 before drawing 0-0 away against the latter last weekend.

According to recent reports, the Black Cats remain inside the Premier League relegation zone, but a renewed sense of resilience has given Le Bris’s side something to build on. Their defensive home form has been particularly pleasing, keeping four clean sheets in their last six home matches across all competitions.

With a tricky trip to Italian giants AC Milan looming on matchday six, Le Bris might view this encounter against Jagiellonia as a must-win opportunity if they wish to climb back into the top eight and ensure they avoid a playoff place.

Competing in the Europa League for the first time in their history this term, Jagiellonia have endured a difficult start to their League Phase campaign, losing three of their first four matches to leave them sitting one point outside of the knockout round playoff places.

The 2024-25 Conference League quarter-finalists responded to a 2-1 opening defeat to Olympiacos with a 3-1 home victory over Ararat-Armenia, but they have since been brought back down to earth by successive losses without scoring against Anderlecht (3-0) and Levski Sofia (1-0).

Thirty-four-year-old boss Adrian Siemieniec is now ready to fulfil one of his coaching “dreams” by taking his Jagiellonia side to a Premier League stadium, with Thursday’s fixture against Sunderland representing one of their toughest tests yet on the continent.

Seeking to avoid a third straight away loss in Europe will be even more challenging without any away supporters, as Jaga were handed a UEFA ban following crowd disturbances in their most recent loss to Levski Sofia.

On the domestic front, Siemieniec recently acknowledged that his team’s form has fallen far below expectations this term, with seven wins and seven defeats posted in 14 Ekstraklasa matches. A 3-1 defeat at KS Cracovia last weekend leaves them down in ninth place in the table, six points behind the top three.

Sunderland form (all competitions):.

Jagiellonia Bialystok Europa League form:.

Jagiellonia Bialystok form (all competitions):.

Sunderland will be without Granit Xhaka (calf), Brian Brobbey, Daniel Ballard, Habib Diarra (all thigh) and Romaine Mundle (knee) due to injury, while Jocelin Ta Bi, Melker Ellborg, Alan Browne and Aji Alese are all ineligible for the Europa League.

Although Trai Hume is one booking away from a European ban, he could continue on the right flank, unless Le Bris decides to recall either Malick Fofana or Nilson Angulo.

Enzo Le Fee has scored a team-high four goals this season – all penalties – and could operate in an advanced midfield role in front of Noah Sadiki and Jules Ahoka, while defensive trio Kevin Danso, Omar Alderete and Dayann Methalie will all be pushing to return after watching on as substitutes against Aston Villa.

As for Jagiellonia Bialystok, Ousmane Sow picked up a knock last weekend and has emerged as a doubt, but Norbert Wojtuszek recovered from injury to feature as an second-half substitute last time out and may be in a position to start at right-back ahead of Rodrigo Conceicao.

Jesus Imaz and Nik Prelec have scored seven goals each this term, but they are yet to make the net ripple in the Europa League this term. Nevertheless, the pair are strong contenders to start in centre-midfield and up front respectively.

Sunderland possible starting lineup:.

Roefs; Meunier, Danso, Alderete, Methalie; Sadiki, Ahoka; Hume, Le Fee, Fofana; Isidor.

Jagiellonia Bialystok possible starting lineup:.

Abramowicz; Wojtuszek, Konstantopoulos, Vital, Montioa; Romanczuk, Klynge, Imaz; Agbonifo, Prelec, Szmyt.

With Sunderland finding the net with just 4.8% of their shots in the League Phase thus far, and failing to score more than once in eight of nine outings at the Stadium of Light this season, their backline should continue to carry the heavy lifting due to persistent struggles in the final third.

Goals are unlikely to flow freely in another finely-balanced encounter on Wearside, but we are still backing Le Bris’s men to navigate their way to a slender victory on home soil.

Manchester United are furious at referees’ chief Howard Webb’s support for the decision to send off Leny Yoro at Liverpool, despite the defender having his one-match suspension removed.

The French centre-back was dismissed after only eight minutes of United’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield on Sunday for fouling Reds striker Alexander Isak as he advanced towards goal, with referee Sam Barrott deciding Yoro had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

United successfully appealed for wrongful dismissal and the suspension has now been removed, the Football Association has confirmed, meaning Yoro is free to play in the Premier League match against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Liverpool scored their opening goal directly from the free-kick awarded for Yoro’s challenge.

Sources indicate that one question raised was whether Isak had the ball sufficiently under control for this to count as denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity. The Swede’s touch took the ball into the arms of United goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

Pro Ref’s chief refereeing officer Webb backed the decision to dismiss the 21-year-old, saying it was “certainly not clearly wrong”.

However, United boss Mauricio Pochettino vehemently disagreed and hit out at the lack of VAR intervention.

It is understood that the club are unhappy with Webb’s comments and plan to make their feelings known to Pro Ref.

Recent findings suggest that speaking at a press conference ahead of his team’s Champions League match against Sporting in Lisbon on Wednesday, the Argentinian said: “Very disappointed. My question always was the same, we can accept the referee can make a mistake because of the emotion of the game, sometimes the view or the position can affect that. But if we have VAR, what were they doing?

“Now, are we going to repeat the game? Are we going to have the possibility to play with similar tools – 11 v 11?

Sources indicate that “We have an unbelievable car, but we need to have the level to drive, we need to drive in the best way. We love the technology, yes, and we accept the technology is there, but what are they doing? But it’s not only this mistake, it affects everything.

“No-one is talking about the [Dominik Szoboszlai’s] goal wasn’t legal, they should have disallowed the goal because [Bradley] Barcola was touching our wall. Maybe in the last two years the rules have changed while I was in America. Why didn’t they check it? It must be disallowed.”.

Webb discussed the sending-off with former Liverpool and United striker Michael Owen in the latest edition of Match Officials: Mic’d Up, which aired on Tuesday evening but was recorded before the FA confirmed Yoro’s suspension had been removed.

“The reason we’re talking about it is the fourth consideration [in DOGSO decisions], that’s control or likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball,” Webb remarked.

“Isak’s got control of the ball, he’s got possession, he’s got the touch, he knocks it past Yoro. He’s moving at pace at that moment and a crowd comes in and knocks him down.

“There’s a question mark I guess around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would.

“The VAR checks to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect, and formed the opinion that it wasn’t.

According to recent reports, “I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it’s a little bit debatable. (It’s) certainly not clearly wrong.”.

VAR John Brooks was of the same opinion as he stated in the audio between him and referee Barrott: “Let’s roll it through firstly to see whether the attacker is going to get on the end of the ball.

“Just roll through real speed. So, at full speed, Isak maintains his momentum and likely gets on the end of it.

“OK, certainly not clearly wrong that he doesn’t. So I think the DOGSO confirmed.”.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Europa League tie between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium.

According to recent reports, back in 2008, Bournemouth’s prospect of a European meeting with Milan seemed impossible. After entering administration with crippling debts of around £4m, Bournemouth were handed a 10-point deduction and relegated from League One. To make matters worse, a hefty 17-point deduction was given to the club ahead of the 2008-09 League Two season, with relegation to non-league seeming inevitable. However, midway through the campaign, the transformative Eddie Howe was parachuted in as Bournemouth’s saviour, eventually guiding the club to safety.

According to recent reports, fast forward to October 2026 in an extraordinary rise and Bournemouth are competing in their first-ever European campaign in the club’s 127-year existence. They welcome Milan to Dorset, having earned back-to-back victories over Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz to kick off their inaugural Europa League adventure in style.

Now, they host the second most successful side in the European Cup history. In terms of heritage and silverware, these clubs could not be further apart, but on the pitch, it’s incredibly tough to call.

On Sunday, Marco Rose’s Bournemouth picked up their first Premier League win of the season, beating 10-man Sunderland 2-0 at the Vitality thanks to goals from Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson to move out of the relegation zone.

Milan lost their opening Europa League fixture 2-0 at home to Benfica, before battering Salzburg 4-0 in Austria, with Alphadjo Cisse netting a stunning hat-trick.

In a recent development, crystal Palace are also in the Europa League tonight and face an incredibly daunting away trip to Turkish side Besiktas. Palace lost 3-2 to Sage’s former employers Lyon in their previous Europa League outing, with a positive performance and result needed to restore the fans’ faith.

Cesc Fabregas has praised Massimiliano Alvini for the way he set Frosinone up against AC Milan, despite their heavy defeat.

According to recent reports, there has been a divided narrative after Milan put five goals past Frosinone at San Siro on Sunday night, the team that have been one of the surprise packages in Serie A so far this season. Some feel Alvini was too aggressive in his approach, while others praised his unwavering principles.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It is not too dissimilar to some of the discourse that has followed Fabregas around early in his coaching career. The exchange between the Spaniard and Massimiliano Allegri made the headlines last season, after Milan’s more pragmatic approach yielded four points against the Lariani.

Speaking at a press conference on the eve of the Champions League match against AEK Athens, Fabregas also answered a question about his style of play and gave a nod to Alvini. His words are via MilanPress.

“I want to continue to hear that Alvini is a great coach. He is. In the press conference he said he’ll never change, and for me that means identity, courage, and knowing what you want to do,” he began.

“It’s very key, even when you win or lose 1-0 or not. You’re not bad when you lose, you’re not a phenomenon when you win. I’ll do the same as he did against Milan, I’ll stick with my ideas.

“Obviously, there are games where you don’t play well, you have to know how to manage them when you’re not at your best. But I can’t change everything that’s good here.”.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri.

Here was Arsenal’s very own Groundhog Day.

Mikel Arteta would have feared what was coming as the misses piled up and his team found increasingly remarkable ways to not score.

Gyokeres nets stunner as Arsenal held by Dortmund in thriller.

Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund LIVE: Latest score and updates Champions League.

Man Utd make Pro Ref decision amid Pochettino red card rage.

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway.

According to recent reports, it was rinse and repeat from an Arsenal perspective. Completely dominate the opening 45 minutes with some sublime football. Take the lead but then fail to kick on. Drop the intensity in the second half and regret those missed opportunities.

That happened against Slavia Prague, when the Gunners just about held on in the second half to win. It happened on Saturday, when they had to come from behind just to draw a match they should have been three or four goals up in.

Sources indicate that and it happened here, in perhaps the most ridiculous way yet. With some better decision-making in the final third, the Premier League champions might have put six past Dortmund.

Instead, from their 30 shots, Arsenal managed just four shots on target and one goal. The visitors rode their luck but they stayed within touch and when their moment came, Maximilian Beier took it with the kind of ruthlessness Arteta can only dream of.

It is unrealistic to expect the north Londoners to dominate a match for the full 90 minutes, even more so against Dortmund than the likes of Slavia Prague and Newcastle.

The problem is Arsenal’s lack of efficiency when they are on top means they cannot afford even the slightest drop in standards or intensity.

Score the two or three goals that the dominance deserves in the first half and a dip after the break will not be so decisive. As it is, with Arsenal leaving the margins so thin, one moment is all it takes for the hard work to be undone.

According to recent reports, at St James’ Park, that moment was Odegaard mis-kicking a clearance. Here, it was Joane Gadou charging away from Christos Tzolis and nobody in the home midfield coming across to cover.

The match should have been done by then. Again, Arsenal were sensational in the first 45 minutes.

Sources indicate that noni Madueke, a constant threat, could not sort his feet out promptly enough when a rebound fell to him. The winger was then completely open, screaming for the ball shortly after when Declan Rice instead went by himself and had his shot deflected wide.

Counters were wasted. Viktor Gyokeres, who opened the scoring with a superb strike from distance, suddenly could not hit the target. When Arsenal went in only 1-0 up, what followed next was as predictable as it was galling for the Gunners.

The level dropped just slightly and the Bundesliga leaders came back into the game, equalising ten minutes after the restart.

Even then, though, Arsenal should have been able to recover. Unlike against Slavia Prague or Newcastle, Arsenal did not fall away for an extended period. This match was there for them to win and the chances came thick and fast.

According to recent reports, gyokeres headed wide from a few yards out. The Arsenal fans spent almost the entire final half an hour screaming at the players to shoot as extra touches were taken around the area.

When Serhou Guirassy then bounced the ball off his body onto his own post not once but twice, Arteta collapsed to the ground in disbelief.

The winner would not come. A top-two finish, which was so vital in last season’s run to the final, has now become much harder.

Industry observers note that but that is what this side keep doing. They seem determined to make things hard for himself. Another match that should have been won inside an hour turned into a 90-minute slugfest.

With Arsenal hoping this is another long season domestically and in Europe, it is a habit they must shake fast.

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 19:19, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 19:21.

Manchester United defender Ayden Heaven is reportedly open to leaving the 20-time English champions on loan during the January transfer window.

Heaven, 20, has made eight appearances for the Red Devils this season, including five outings in the Premier League, but he was an unused substitute against Liverpool on Sunday.

Man United are expected to target a new defender during the January transfer window due to their problems in that area of the field.

The Red Devils have conceded 34 times across all competitions this season, which is the worst defensive record in Europe's top five leagues.

According to BBC Sport, Heaven has concerns over what Man United's current struggles could mean for his development.

Heaven allegedly accepts that current head coach Mauricio Pochettino is likely to turn to more experienced options, as the Red Devils face a battle against relegation from the Premier League.

The Englishman has a contract at Old Trafford until the summer of 2029, but it is understood that he would be willing to leave the club on a permanent basis if the right opportunity arrived.

Heaven is right now with the Man United squad preparing for Wednesday's Champions League contest with Portuguese giants Sporting Lisbon.

However, it would be a surprise to see him named in the starting side, or feature off the bench, especially as Luke Shaw has returned to fitness.

Fulham's Calvin Bassey and Brentford's Nathan Collins are believed to be January options for Man United to boost their defensive unit.

Heaven arrived at Man United from Arsenal in February 2025, and he has represented the 20-time English champions on 32 occasions in all competitions.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that patch: After a delay, the report discussed in this story was released by the US National Academies of Sciences, Engineering and Medicine on 24 November.
  • It has been revealed that science publishers take too long to retract or correct research papers, a report by the US National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (NASEM) finds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A statue of Albert Einstein holding a scientific manuscript sits outside the US National Academy of Sciences building in Washington DC.Credit: Paul J. Richards/AFP via Getty.

Recent findings suggest that patch: After a delay, the report discussed in this story was released by the US National Academies of Sciences, Engineering and Medicine on 24 November. The academies said that the problem was with erroneous references added to the report in response to peer review.

It has been revealed that science publishers take too long to retract or correct research papers, a report by the US National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (NASEM) finds. Standards for fixing errors are also inconsistently applied across journals, it says.

Why retractions data could be a powerful tool for cleaning up science.

Why retractions data could be a powerful tool for cleaning up science.

It has been revealed that there are no data on how long a retraction or correction at the moment takes, because journals do not generally disclose when they were alerted to underlying problems; the NASEM report says that they should start doing this. On average, according to the Retraction Watch database, retractions occur around 2.4 years after a paper is published. The report recommends that, in most cases, editorial review processes be completed within 12 weeks, and should rarely stretch beyond 6 months — at least when editors are looking at concerns over a single paper.

“The massive picture is, the process is too slow,” says Randy Schekman, a cell biologist at the University of California, Berkeley, who chaired the 13-person committee that produced the NASEM report. A prompter and more transparent process would strengthen the reliability of the scientific record, he says.

The report was due to be published online on 19 November but was delayed after journalists at Science noted that it contained some references with fabricated first names for authors, a possible sign that large language models had been used to write or edit the material and that it had been insufficiently checked.

“It’s unfortunate that there were these flawed references in a report about fixing the literature,” notes Jennifer Byrne, a cancer researcher and research-integrity sleuth at the University of Sydney in Australia, who first flagged the concern to Science when reviewing the report, which was shared ahead of publication with media outlets.

The report had two main aims: to speed up the process of retraction or correction and to lower the “tremendous emotional barriers” for authors to correct honest mistakes in the record, Schekman notes. “Part of the problem is that it’s too rare for a paper to be retracted,” he adds.

Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?

Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?

Sources indicate that it also suggests that journals shouldn’t wait for complaints to reach them, but instead “take proactive steps” to identify errors and integrity issues. These might include journal-wide audits, or regularly monitoring social-media feeds and online platforms where post-publication issues are raised, it states.

Existing guidelines for publishers, such as those from the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) in London, urge only a “timely” response to concerns1, without setting out expected schedules, and don’t suggest that journals scan online platforms for complaints.

According to recent reports, “A major theme running through the report is that we have to distinguish between retraction or correction, and research misconduct,” notes Dorothy Bishop, a research-integrity sleuth in Oxford, UK, who was on the NASEM committee. Authors shouldn’t associate a retraction with the stigma of research misconduct, she states. And although journal editors sometimes wait for a university to investigate whether there is misconduct before correcting a paper, they shouldn’t, she adds.

More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a latest record.

More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a new record.

Calls for changing these attitudes aren’t newly introduced: journals have long emphasized that retractions can result from honest mistakes. In a 2022 editorial, Holden Thorp, the editor in chief of Science, urged that the processes of issuing corrections or retractions and making a determination of misconduct should be kept separate2, and COPE guidelines already emphasize the point. But “there are still plenty of people who see a correction or retraction as an allegation of fraud”, says Thorp, who was also on the NASEM committee. “Hopefully, this report will accelerate the recognition of the distinction,” he says.

By Saikat Mandal | 24 Nov 2026 19:25, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 06:17.

Union SG will be looking to maintain their impressive Europa League form when they host Lech Poznan at King Power at Den Dreef Stadium on Thursday.

The Old Lady remain unbeaten in the competition and sit fourth in the standings, while the visitors are languishing second from bottom in the table.

The Belgian side began their Europa League campaign with a convincing 3-0 victory over Viktoria Plzen away from home and have since collected 10 points from four matches, scoring 10 goals in the process.

The only occasion on which they dropped points came against Real Sociedad, when David Hubert's side fought back from behind to secure a 1-1 draw.

A scintillating second-half display helped them to a commanding 4-0 victory over Hapoel Be'er Sheva, while Union followed that up with a 2-1 triumph over Celta Vigo on matchday four.

They are unbeaten in their last 16 matches and head into this encounter on the back of seven consecutive victories across all competitions, a run that should give them plenty of confidence.

USG are also setting the pace in the Pro League, sitting top of the table with 32 points from 12 matches, having recorded 10 wins and two draws without tasting defeat.

Lech Poznan comfortably dispatched Swiss side Thun 9-2 on aggregate to secure their place in the Europa League league phase, but they have since struggled to find their feet in the competition.

The Railwaymen began their campaign with a 4-0 defeat to Crystal Palace before suffering another heavy loss by the same scoreline against Bayer Leverkusen.

The Polish side ground out a hard-fought 1-1 draw against Sunderland, but Benfica proved too strong in their next outing, handing them a 3-1 defeat on matchday four.

Having scored just two goals and conceded 12, they are among the three teams languishing near the bottom of the table with only one point, with only FC Ararat-Armenia faring worse.

Lech Poznan, however, have been outstanding domestically, sitting top of the league with 35 points from 14 matches, four clear of Gornik despite having played a game fewer.

Hubert could make several changes to the side that faced Kortrijk in their last league outing, with Nikki Havenaar potentially coming into a three-man defence and Louis Patris moving into midfield.

Besfort Zeneli, who scored twice against Celta Vigo, is likely to return to the starting lineup in place of Darius Olaru, while Kevin Rodríguez is expected to lead the line.

Lech Poznan, meanwhile, are likely to adopt a more cautious approach away from home, with Niels Frederiksen potentially setting his side up in a 4-2-3-1 formation, with Yannick Agnero operating as the lone striker.

Mateusz Pruchniewski has been ruled out for the rest of the season with an ACL injury, while Ali Gholizadeh is still recovering from the same problem and is unlikely to return before January.

Alex Douglas is sidelined with a broken rib, while Joao Moutinho is not expected to return before February. However, Pablo Rodriguez and Mikael Ishak have both returned to training.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Villarreal have rubbished a bizarre online rumour claiming Nicolas Pepe required eye surgery after he filmed himself taking in the solar eclipse.

Reports circulating on social media over the weekend suggested Pepe had sustained damage to his retina during the lunar event back in August, which had supposedly forced the forward to miss five matches.

A resurfaced video, which Pepe himself had uploaded to Snapchat, showed the 31-year-old winger observing the eclipse in Spain without the use of protective glasses.

Industry observers note that ‘To all the idiots on my Snapchat, that is a solar eclipse! In France, all they got was a little croissant from the bakery,’ Pepe joked at the time.

Unsurprisingly, the wild rumour promptly spread online amongst fans, many of whom mocked Pepe for apparently going against the advice of experts and wilfully exposing himself to intense visible light, ultraviolet and infrared radiation.

But on Sunday evening, Pepe’s club Villarreal released a statement vehemently denying these baseless claims on social media.

‘Villarreal CF, in response to reports published in various media outlets recently, clarifies that it is completely false that Nicolas Pepe’s eye surgery has any connection to observing the solar eclipse,’ the statement from the La Liga outfit read.

Villarreal confirmed that Pepe had indeed undergone surgery but stressed that it was ‘entirely unrelated’ to the solar eclipse.

‘The surgery had been scheduled in advance for reasons entirely unrelated to this event,’ the statement continued.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘The club urges accuracy and responsibility when reporting on matters related to its players’ health.’.

The surgery Pepe underwent meant the ex-Arsenal attacker was sidelined for Villarreal’s games against Real Madrid, Napoli, Elche, Liverpool and Valencia last month.

The Ivory Coast international made his return in Villarreal’s Copa del Rey first-round tie with Manacor, in which he scored his side’s final goal in a thumping 5-0 victory.

He has gone on to feature in all of Villarreal’s next four matches, although he has failed to complete 90 minutes in any of those contests.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Since joining Villarreal from Trabzonspor back in 2024, Pepe has made a total of 86 appearances for the Spanish club, chipping in with 14 goals and 18 assists in that time.

Villarreal surrendered an early two-goal lead to lose 3-2 at Barcelona on Sunday and sit tenth in La Liga after 13 matches.

Pepe became Arsenal’s club-record signing when he signed from Lille for a fee of £72million back in 2019 – and the move remains the third most expensive deal in the Gunners’ history, behind those involving Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes.

Despite enjoying an encouraging start, Pepe badly struggled to live up to expectations at the Emirates and has often been branded one of the worst signings of the Premier League era.

Sources indicate that I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

Arsenal were fortunate not to concede a penalty against Borussia Dortmund during their Champions League draw.

The Premier League champions and Bundesliga leaders held each other to a 1-1 stalemate at the Emirates Stadium, as Viktor Gyokeres’ rifled opener was cancelled out in the second half by Maximilian Beier.

It was the Gunners’ second draw on the spin after a 2-2 encounter at St James’ Park, where Noni Madueke rescued a point against Newcastle after Malick Thiaw and Harvey Barnes had put the Magpies ahead following Eberechi Eze’s opening goal.

But it was the goalscorer Gyokeres who almost turned from hero to villain, as he allegedly handled a Dortmund corner in the second period.

It led Amazon Prime Video pundits Alan Shearer and Mark Clattenberg to question referee Maurizio Mariani’s decision not to award a spot kick to the visitors.

“I think Arsenal were fortunate to have gotten away with that one,” Shearer said on co-commentary.

"I know it might have been Fabio Silva in front of him trying to flick it on, but he didn't, and his arm is actually out.".

Clattenberg, said alongside the record Premier League goalscorer in the north London gantry, concurred.

"We all know UEFA have a stricter handball rule than we see in the Premier League, but what doesn't save Gyokeres in this situation is, the ball comes in from a distance and he makes a little movement of his arm towards the ball so that makes it look more like a penalty kick for me,” the former official noted.

Former Arsenal forward Theo Walcott spoke of his relief at the penalty not being given.

"As soon as it hit his hand, straight away my heart is in my mouth, I think it's a penalty," he said.

"I think he's got away with that. I'm pleased it wasn't given because it's not a penalty, but in Europe it probably should be.".

Gyokeres asserted his innocence in his post-match interview.

"I think the arm was towards my body," the Swede mentioned.

‘Wake up,’ squawked Gary Neville as he released into an evisceration of a Manchester United defence that had just capitulated in all too familiar fashion.

The Anfield washing machine, as Mikel Arteta once described Liverpool’s fortress, has accounted for sterner rearguards than the one Mauricio Pochettino has inherited, but there was something particularly abject about this particular 4-0 humbling.

Whether it was the grim acceptance that the eventual scoreline was deemed passable after the most farcical of beginnings to a United managerial tenure, or the immediate removal of any notion that Pochettino has a honeymoon period to enjoy, Neville struggled to compute the reality of the league table as it stands.

‘You play for Man Utd,’ Neville barked, having slapped himself in the face, in surprisingly aggressive fashion, to symbolise the wake-up call his club are in need of.

While he provided an early frontrunner for meme of the season, Neville failed to grasp the full gravity of the situation Pochettino has landed himself in.

Considering the likelihood of United finding themselves in a fully-fledged battle to preserve their Premier League status, Neville was dismissive to the point of arrogance.

‘I don’t believe they’re in a relegation fight,’ he stated, without providing a modicum of evidence to explain his confidence.

Industry observers note that 🚨| WATCH: Gary Neville has had ENOUGH, slapping himself in the face live on TV after another Manchester United loss. 😳 pic.twitter.com/UovS3bApRk.

‘It’s as bad as it’s been for 55 years but I do think they’ll come out of it and move up the table.’.

Listing the likes of Andrey Santos, unable to nail down a starting slot since his £48million move from Chelsea, Amad Diallo, no Premier League goal in approaching a year, Patrick Dorgu, without a place in the redundant wing-back role he was recruited to fill in Ruben Amorim’s doomed system, and Bryan Mbeumo, immediately sacrificed when United were reduced to 10 men yesterday, as the players best suited to fulfil the requirements of Pochettino’s high-intensity ethos should have prompted an immediate Neville U-turn, even before he threw the name of Bruno Fernandes into the mix, while adding the caveat that ‘he can run around, but whether he knows where he’s running is a bit more debatable’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Make no mistake about it, United are in a dogfight and the situation will only deteriorate further if the dressing room shares Neville’s assertion that this group of players are too good to go down.

Time on the training ground to organise a defence that is now officially the worst in Europe’s top five league is limited and while January will surely bring reinforcements, there is precious little to suggest United have either the funds, or a cohesive enough recruitment strategy to identify the players they require if they are to dig themselves out of trouble.

Sitting second bottom after 11 games is not a small sample size to be dealing with either, especially when you consider the majority of these players were in-part responsible for the multitude of unwanted records that were broken during Amorim’s wretched stint.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It should also be remembered that Spurs had 18 points after 11 games last season and only stayed up on the final day. United have eight points and have already been beaten by two goals or more on six occasions this term in all competitions.

While Neville’s sparring partner Jamie Carragher may have gotten a little ahead of himself in terms of where Liverpool are at this juncture in Andoni Iraola’s rebuild, he was on the money when assessing how United compare to the teams they should be focused on competing with at present.

‘No-one believes they are, no-one will say that they are (in a relegation fight),’ he mentioned. ‘But the strength of the Premier League this season, what we could call teams that we expect to be mid-table or near the bottom, I think it’s as strong as it’s ever been.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We can talk about teams at the top and say it’s nowhere near as strong. Think about teams in the Champions League. Our teams in this league are not in the top four or five in the Champions League, I don’t think. But when you look at the Europa League or Conference League, we expect our teams to walk it!

Sources indicate that ‘Look at Fulham, going away to Manchester City, 1-1. Leeds go to Chelsea, 4-1. There are no poor teams. There aren’t many great teams in the league but there are no poor teams. And that’s a problem for Man United.

Sources indicate that ‘Their next league game is Brentford at home. Manchester United are one of the biggest clubs in the world, Brentford are well-run. If Man United beat Brentford at home, I think we’d all look at that and say ‘great result.’ That will not be an easy game.

In a recent development, he added: ‘The only game they’ve won is Ipswich, a newly-promoted team. In that game they went 1-0 down, Ipswich had another chance. That’s the only game they’ve won.’.

Indeed, United are second bottom, not second top, and until everyone connected with the club accepts that reality and accepts last season’s Michael Carrick-inspired renaissance for what it was, a flash in the pan, the route out of this mess will be a bumpy one.

  • Braga will look to strengthen their position in the Conference League knockout-stage race when they welcome KuPS Kuopio to the Estadio Municipal de Braga on Thursday evening.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 24 Nov 2026 19:40.

Braga will look to strengthen their position in the Conference League knockout-stage race when they welcome KuPS Kuopio to the Estadio Municipal de Braga on Thursday evening.

Franclim Carvalho's side are 17th in the 36-team standings with four points from three matches, while the Finnish visitors sit 33rd with just one point after failing to win any of their opening three European outings.

Despite going unbeaten in their six matches across three Conference League qualifying rounds (W4, D2) and keeping clean sheets in all of them, Braga have found life in the league phase considerably more challenging.

The Archbishops began their campaign with a disappointing 3-0 defeat away to Copenhagen before responding with a 2-0 home victory over Gent on matchday two, giving Carvalho his first win since replacing the sacked Carlos Vicens in October.

However, Braga were unable to build on that success in their latest continental outing, playing out a goalless draw away to Aarhus, although the new manager can take encouragement from the defensive improvements made in recent times.

The Portuguese outfit are unbeaten in their last four matches across all competitions, keeping clean sheets in each and winning three, with their latest success coming in a 2-0 victory away to Vitoria de Guimaraes in the Taca de Portugal at the weekend.

That result followed a 1-0 league win at Rio Ave, leaving Braga eighth in the Primeira Liga table with 17 points from their opening 11 fixtures and three points adrift of the top five.

The Archbishops are also three points away from fifth place in the Conference League standings, with several teams between 10th and 14th sitting just two points ahead, meaning maximum points on Thursday could strengthen their hopes of securing a top-eight finish.

Braga have plenty of reason to feel confident ahead of the contest, having won 14 of their last 16 home matches in European competition (D1, L1) and kept 12 clean sheets during that run.

KuPS, meanwhile, have struggled to make an impression in their second consecutive Conference League league-phase campaign, losing 4-2 to Trabzonspor in their opening fixture before suffering a 2-0 defeat away to Borac Banja Luka on matchday two.

The Finnish side collected their first point with a goalless draw against Gent on matchday three, but that result did little to disguise their attacking struggles, having scored just twice and conceded six goals across their opening three matches in the competition.

Miika Nuutinen's men have also gone seven matches without a victory, including a 1-1 draw against Swedish side Norrkoping in a friendly on November 19, while their most recent competitive outing was a 2-0 home defeat to Inter Turku in their final match of the 2026 top-flight campaign.

That result left the Yellow-Blacks third in the Veikkausliiga table, meaning they missed out on retaining the domestic title they won last season but secured a place in the first qualifying round of the Conference League.

KuPS have also struggled on their travels, recording just one victory in their last eight competitive away matches and failing to win any of their most recent four, three of which ended in defeat.

Braga will be without Sikou Niakate, who is recovering from a ruptured Achilles tendon that has kept him sidelined since April.

Jonas Wind is also doubtful after missing the recent victory over Vitoria because of physical overload, while Gabriel Silva returned as a second-half substitute at the weekend after missing the previous four matches through fitness problems and could feature again as he builds up his match fitness.

Fran Navarro ended a more than three-month wait for a goal by scoring against Vitoria and is expected to retain his place at the head of the attack, with club captain Ricardo Horta and Pau Victor also likely to feature in Carvalho's forward line.

KuPS could be without 22-year-old Ghanaian winger Bob Nii Armah, who picked up an injury during the goalless draw with Gent.

Thirty-three-year-old attacker Piotr Parzyszek has started all three of the Finnish side's league-phase matches and could retain his place despite failing to score in his last 10 competitive appearances for the club.

Braga possible starting lineup:.

B Fontes; V Gomez, Lagerbielke, Barisic, Travassos; Gorby, Dorgeles, Moutinho; P Victor, Navarro, Horta.

Kreidl; Savolainen, Hamalainen, Lotjonen, Kujasalo; Gasc, Pasanen; Aiki, Pennanen, Eskesen; Parzyszek.

KuPS have managed just two goals in three Conference League matches and enter this encounter without a win in six outings, while Braga have won three of their last four matches and kept clean sheets in all of them, making a home victory the most likely outcome.

However, it was an improvement on Kepa’s display in the Carabao Cup final last season and solid enough to be confident he will keep his place over Illan Meslier while Raya remains out.

Kepa has had limited football since joining the club, so trusted has Raya become for Arsenal, but Arteta insisted he will have full faith in the goalkeeper if he is required to start in goal against City.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Moroccan FA say they proposal to explore all legal avenues to appeal after expressing their “protest” against the CAS ruling to reinstate Senegal as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners.

While Senegal won 1-0 against Morocco in the final of AFCON 2025, the match was beset by controversy. Senegal players and staff left the pitch in the 98th minute in protest against the award of a penalty for the hosts, which left the game paused for 14 minutes. The match eventually resumed, Brahim Diaz missed the spot kick and the game went to extra time, which saw Senegal score and go on to lift the trophy.

Sources indicate that but African football governing body CAF retrospectively awarded the title to Morocco two months after the final, stating that Senegal’s conduct during the match had disqualified them as winners. Morocco were named automatic 3-0 winners.

The Senegalese FA took an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) which, after a months-long saga, reinstated Senegal as champions on Tuesday.

But Morocco have not given up, citing reports of an alleged telephone conversation between CAS panelist Ulrich Haas and the president of Senegal’s football federation hours before Tuesday’s ruling as one reason they have grounds for an appeal.

Sources indicate that the CAS ruling said: “The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF, in French) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025 (AFCON 2025). The decision rendered by the CAF Appeal Board is set aside and the decision by the CAF Disciplinary Board is reinstated.

“Consequently, the result obtained at the end of the AFCON 2025 final is confirmed (1-0 for Senegal).

“By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume.

“In the Panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee’s decision were limited to the pitch. As such, the Panel considers that the Referee’s decision was covered by the "field of play" doctrine.

“Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case.”.

In this context, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest at the failure to take into account its demand to arrange the necessary legal consequences for practices that would compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure, especially what has been confirmed regarding communication between the German referee Ulrich Haas (who sat on the CAS panel) and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.

“The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and FIFA, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties.

Head coach Fabian Hurzeler rued his side’s “missed opportunity which can't happen again” after seeing leaders Arsenal and Man City also drop points over the weekend. Brighton still sit between both clubs in second place in the table, six points behind the Gunners and level on points with City in third.

Brighton have scored a whopping 40 goals in 18 games across all competitions this term, but the goals have dried up slightly in recent weeks; they have drawn a blank in front of goal in three of their last seven games and have scored at least twice on just two occasions during this run.

While the prospect of qualifying for next season’s Champions League via their domestic performances has become a distinct possibility, Brighton also have aspirations of winning their first-ever major trophy and following in the footsteps of Crystal Palace, West Ham and Chelsea in winning the Conference League this term.

The Seagulls, who secured a narrow 1-0 win over Getafe in Spain three weeks ago, currently sit fifth in the 36-team League Phase standings and could consolidate their place in the top eight with a victory on Thursday.

Should they beat Craiova without reply, they will become just the third English team this century to prevail in five consecutive European home games without conceding a goal.

Universitatea Craiova narrowly missed out on a place in the Conference League knockout rounds last season, finishing outside the top-24 positions on goal difference after accumulating seven points from six matches.

However, the White-Blues have already picked up the same number of points in half as many games so far this season and sit eighth in the table, leaving them well-placed to secure a historic first-ever appearance in the knockout stages of UEFA competition and potentially bypass the playoff round altogether.

After holding Getafe to a 1-1 draw on matchday one, Filipe Coelho’s side have since celebrated back-to-back wins over Andorran outfit Inter Escaldes (3-1) and Albanian team Egnatia (1-0) – they have not won three consecutive European games since a four-match streak in the 1984 UEFA Cup.

Craiova travel to the South Coast of England in superb form, having put together an impressive 15-game unbeaten run in all tournaments (W11 D4), most recently winning 6-2 against UTA Arad last weekend to retain their position at the top of the Romanian Superliga table.

Brighton quintet Kaoru Mitoma (hamstring), Evan Ferguson (ankle), Malick Yalcouye, Stefanos Tzimas (both knee) and Zadok Yohanna (thigh) remain sidelined with injuries, while Jaouen Hadjam (knee) will be assessed ahead of kickoff.

Femi Azeez was “available” to face Hull at the weekend but was not selected in the matchday squad. The summer signing from Millwall recently recovered from a thigh injury and could be ready to make his long-awaited debut for the Seagulls on Thursday.

Brighton’s Jack Hinshelwood has scored each of his last five goals for Brighton on home soil and could be recalled to the first XI along with the likes of Ferdi Kadioglu, Mats Wieffer, Ibrahim Osman and Charalampos Kostoulas.

As for Universitatea Craiova, Monday Etim (muscle) and Pavlo Isenko (knee) are both ruled out with injuries, while Mihnea Radulescu is ineligible for the Conference League.

Coelho is expected to stick with a 3-4-3 formation, with Oleksandr Romanchuk, Nikola Stevanovic and Vladimir Screciu set to continue in a three-man backline as Nicusor Bancu and Carlos Mora operating as wing-backs.

Stefan Baiaram scored a brace at the weekend and could retain his starting spot on the left side of attack, while Simon Elisor and Assad Al-Hamlawi have both netted 11 goals this season and will battle it out for a start up front.

Universitatea Craiova possible starting lineup:.

Popescu; Romanchuk, Stevanovic, Screciu; Mora, Baluta, Cicaldau, Bancu; Matei, Al Hamlawi, Baiaram.

As the only team yet to concede in this season’s Conference League, and with nine of their last 10 home outings seeing at least one side fail to score, Brighton possess the defensive solidity to frustrate an in-form Craiova attack.

The Romanian leaders are set for by far their sternest examination on the continent, and even if Hurzeler opts to shuffle his pack, the Seagulls should have more than enough quality to claim a routine victory.

Latest Update: Sleuth finds ‘impossible proteins’ in hundreds of research papers

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (934 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature
