💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that some studies show the expression of proteins such as caspase-3 (pictured) in cell lines that should not be able to produce them.
  • A scientific sleuth has identified more than 220 research papers that describe impossible patterns of protein expression in genetically altered cell lines.
  • Journals are now taking action to clean up the literature by retracting or correcting the work, and researchers warn that there are probably many more affected studies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that some studies show the expression of proteins such as caspase-3 (pictured) in cell lines that should not be able to produce them. Credit: Dr Mark J. Winter/SPL.

A scientific sleuth has identified more than 220 research papers that describe impossible patterns of protein expression in genetically altered cell lines. In these studies, particular proteins show up in imaging experiments, even though the cells do not have the gene necessary to make them.

Journals are now taking action to clean up the literature by retracting or correcting the work, and researchers warn that there are probably many more affected studies.

Industry observers note that “This problem will not go away,” says Thierry Soussi, a cancer geneticist at Uppsala University in Sweden, who notes that there are several other examples of the issue in now-retracted papers that were not included in the sleuth’s analysis. “This is only the tip of a gigantic iceberg.”.

Industry observers note that cell lines are groups of cells derived from a single origin cell and cultured for use in experiments. Some cancer cell lines have been genetically modified with mutations and deletions — often to remove genes that usually control cell division. This means that the cultures continually divide and grow, giving researchers the chance to study tumour progression and test potential treatments.

The MCF-7 cell line is one of these. It lacks the gene for caspase-3 protein, which is involved in cell death. In 2009, researchers warned1 that some studies that report working with MCF-7 have mysteriously observed caspase-3 expression in western blots, an imaging technique that identifies proteins on the basis of their molecular weight.

Sleuth identifies dozens of studies that used the wrong antibody.

Sleuth identifies dozens of studies that used the wrong antibody.

In the most recent analysis, published as a preprint on 21 October to the data repository Zenodo2, Sholto David, a sleuth based in Arbroath, UK, finds that this problem persists and extends to other cell lines.

David compiled a list of 20 commonly used cell lines with genetic mutations or deletions that leave cells unable to express specific proteins. He then scoured the literature using Google text and image searches to identify examples of western-blot images that unexpectedly identify these proteins. He also searched a collection of 140,000 articles that he had previously downloaded and screened for image-integrity issues and other problems, most of which were biomedicine papers.

He found 230 reports of phantom proteins across 221 papers published since 2004. The most common errors were observations of caspase-3 expression in the MCF-7 cell line, affecting 49 papers; expression of the cell-death protein BAX in the Jurkat cell line in 47 papers; and expression of the signalling protein STAT3 in the PC-3 cell line in 35 papers.

According to recent reports, david suggests several explanations for these impossible protein-expression patterns. They might be the result of honest errors: researchers could have misidentified the cell lines or contaminated them with others. Or the antibodies used to identify proteins in the western-blot experiments could have been non-specific and bound to another protein with the same molecular weight. In fact, David claims that he stumbled across the anomalous proteins while working on a project that flagged hundreds of studies that used the wrong antibodies in experiments.

Another possibility is that some of the papers are the product of paper mills, companies that fabricate and sell scientific manuscripts. David says that some papers in the cache contain the hallmarks of being produced by such outfits, including duplicated images or text templates that are similar to other papers. The proportion of the papers that fall into this category is not clear, he says.

Nature has contacted several authors of papers containing anomalies to ask for comment, but none responded.

A defiant Michael Carrick refused to rule out stripping Bruno Fernandes of the captaincy as the Manchester United manager told his players to cut out their public sniping and start doing their talking on the pitch.

Carrick struck a bullish tone as he came out fighting and moved to reassert his authority after a tumultuous past fortnight that has left him battling to save his job ahead of Sunday’s must-win game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

The United manager began his press conference on Friday afternoon with a stirring five-and-a-half-minute monologue in which he issued an emotional call to arms to his players to demonstrate the values of hard work, sacrifice, humility and resilience that define the club.

Referencing Sir Matt Busby, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton, Ryan Giggs and Wayne Rooney, Carrick warned there could be no “entitlement” culture in echoes of complaints from his predecessor Ruben Amorim.

United are actively considering their options in the event Carrick cannot promptly arrest a shocking start to the season that hit a upcoming low with Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation by Como. The likes of Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe, Unai Emery, Fabian Hürzeler and Antonio Conte are in the frame.

But Carrick insisted he was “100 per cent” convinced he was the right man to take United forward and, while he claimed the dressing room was “not divided”, he has had to contend with first defender Lisandro Martínez and then Fernandes venting in public.

Martínez was fined and publicly apologised for an extraordinary tirade at Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the Old Trafford board last week before Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the Como debacle.

Carrick responded at the time to having his set-up and approach questioned by suggesting tactics count for little if players are unprepared to run.

Asked if he would consider taking the captaincy off Fernandes, Carrick said: “I’m just saying I’ll always – whatever the situation is – do what’s best for the club.”.

Pressed on whether Fernandes’s comments were all the more insidious and divisive at a time when the manager was trying to pull the squad together so soon after Martínez’s outburst, Carrick added: “Yeah, the most important thing for me is the team.

It has been revealed that “First and foremost is the squad, the dynamics in the squad. And again, it’s about the club. And I’ll always do what’s best for the club.”.

Carrick, Wilcox and United chief executive Omar Berrada held a meeting with Martínez in the wake of his criticism but the manager would not be drawn on whether he had spoken with Fernandes and it remains to be seen if he will be captain or start against Bournemouth.

“If I’ve spoken to him or haven’t spoken to him, I don’t think this is the time to go into too much detail,” he mentioned.

In a recent development, carrick agreed that United collectively needed to stop turning on each other in public. “We need to move forward in the right direction. We need to do things that enable us to do that. That’s pretty clear,” he said.

“It [the dressing room] is not divided, no. We just need to get back to doing what we do best and we will.”.

Separately, Carrick expressed sympathy for Fernandes over the “awful” burglary at his home on Wednesday night when he was in Italy, and said the club “are doing a lot of work to support Bruno and his family”.

Carrick is under huge pressure heading into Bournemouth but mentioned he was happy to take the heat if it enabled his players to perform.

“It is my responsibility whatever goes on the pitch, and what we are as a group, and what we look like, and what we feel like,” he said. “I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and for everyone else to stay dry.”.

It has been revealed that nonetheless, Carrick admitted he was “hurting an awful lot” and that the team had to get back to showing the values and qualities that have underpinned the club’s historic success after a “really unacceptable” performance against Como and wider struggles. United have won two of 11 matches this season.

It has been revealed that “I’m not entitled to be here,” Carrick said. “We’re not entitled to win. We’ve won in the past, we’ve got an incredible history, but that doesn’t mean you’re entitled to just win.

Industry observers note that “I’m fully aware of that. It takes hard work, a lot of sacrifice. You’ve got to invest yourself in the club and you’ve got to do a lot of things that maybe aren’t so nice, but you’ve got to do it for each other, and you’ve got to win.

“It’s vital we live up to that, and it’s important for me to push those values, and for our supporters to feel that moving forward.

In a recent development, “We’ve kind of lost our way a bit if I’m honest, and we will get it back. I’m totally confident we’ll get it back. Respect this club, respect what it takes, because it’s very crucial to me.”.

Carrick added that he was inspired by the values of “humility, hard work, resilience, sacrifice and pride” embodied by the likes of Busby, Ferguson, Charlton, Giggs and Rooney.

In a recent development, “We can never lose that, and I won’t let us lose that,” he said. “We’ve had it for a spell, I feel very strongly about that. It inspires me a lot to live up to that and keep driving that with the players.

Recent findings suggest that “There’s a resilience about this club that’s been shown for a long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, success, sustaining success, there’s a resilience in this club that runs very deep.”.

The Argentine has arrived as the fresh Red Devils boss and took charge of his first game on Sunday, which did not go well at all as Liverpool romped to a 4-0 win over their old rivals at Anfield.

Leny Yoro was shown an early red card, leaving Pochettino’s intends in tatters as defeat left Manchester United 19th in the Premier League table.

With just one win and 23 goals conceded in 11 league outings, there have been calls for signings to be made, especially in defence.

Before Pochettino was appointed, club legend Gary Neville even urged him to turn down the job unless the hierarchy promised to sign two defenders over the winter transfer window.

That may still happen, but it will have to be some canny business as the Daily Mail reports that Manchester United will have ‘well under £50 million’ to spend in the next transfer window.

Having focused on midfield signings over the summer, United want a centre-back, left-back and striker, but obviously that cannot be done to any level of quality on such a meagre budget.

Brentford centre-back Nathan Collins has been touted as a target, but the 25-year-old would not be a cheap option.

The Bees paid £23m for him when they signed him from Wolves three years ago and he remains under contract until 2029.

Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has been linked with a move to Old Trafford, having worked with Pochettino in his stint as USA manager.

The former Arsenal man came close to joining Everton in a £40m deal over the summer before the deal collapsing at the last minute.

Manchester United may look to make a loan signing to keep costs down, although could stretch the budget if they feel that relegation is a genuine threat.

Ex-England striker Carlton Cole has slammed Manchester United’s recruitment under INEOS and claims it was ‘criminal’ the club didn’t explore a move for Danny Welbeck in the summer.

There had been a sense of optimism amongst United’s fanbase heading into the season after Michael Carrick picked up the pieces from Ruben Amorim’s turbulent reign to lead the club to a third-place finish last term.

But the Red Devils once again find themselves in a state of disarray after a wretched start to the 2026/27 campaign, which ultimately cost Carrick his job earlier this month.

With genuine fears growing that United could become embroiled in a relegation scrap, Mauricio Pochettino has been tasked with steadying the ship and steering a dispirited squad away from the bottom of the Premier League table.

The Argentine’s tenure got off to a nightmare start at the weekend, though, as his side were put to the sword at the hands of arch-rivals Liverpool in a thumping 4-0 defeat at Anfield.

Sunday’s result ensured United remain firmly in the drop zone after 11 matches, only one point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace with the worst defensive record of any team in Europe’s top five leagues.

If Pochettino was expecting to be supported with significant financial backing in his efforts to turn United’s fortunes around this winter, he will likely be disappointed.

After all, Reports this week suggest the 54-year-old will have a budget of ‘well under £50million’ to work with when the January transfer window opens for business.

Recent findings suggest that asked what Pochettino must address with his meagre funds while tackling United’s woes on The Dressing Room Podcast, Cole replied: ‘The spine. They haven’t got a striker, a worthy striker.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Midfield, I think they’re alright there for now because they’ve got Carlos Baleba and I think he’s a fantastic player by the way, they’ve got Kobbie Mainoo, Bruno Fernandes… I think they’re alright in that position.

Industry observers note that ‘I know the boy from Chelsea, Andrey Santos, he’s there, but I know he’s not tuned in yet because it’s high pressure right now and he’s a little bit off it. They’ve got Youri Tielemans as well. Then you’ve got the centre-backs…’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to Cole, United missed a trick when they gave Chelsea a free run at signing Welbeck from Brighton in the summer.

‘I think it’s criminal they didn’t sign Welbeck,’ he added.

In a recent development, ‘I think he’s wasted at Chelsea at the moment, they should have signed Welbeck. He’d have done alright!’.

Eyebrows were raised when Pochettino named his team to face Liverpool on Sunday, with Matthijs de Ligt thrown in for his first Premier League start of the campaign.

There were signs of rustiness in De Ligt’s game from minute one and it was the Dutchman’s calamitous defending that led to Dominik Szoboszlai’s breakthrough – and Leny Yoro’s sending off – after only ten minutes.

‘I thought that was him [Pochettino] protesting already,’ Cole remarked of De Ligt’s surprise selection.

It has been revealed that ‘I think it was on the first or second day that he was in, he was already saying he wanted more control in the transfer market. I thought you negotiated that in your deal!

‘He’s chosen the right time to do it [make a protest], in a game like that.

‘This was a free hit for him and yes, he needs defenders. But I’ve remarked it before, INEOS have gone with signing forward first and then the next window they get a midfielder… who does that? So that’s what has happened.’.

Cole went a step further on Pochettino’s decision to field De Ligt, adding: ‘I think it’s bang out of order, he’s been stitched up.

Sources indicate that ‘He’s obviously not fit, he can’t read it. When you’ve been out so long, you get your bearings wrong, you don’t know where you are on the pitch. It happens, right? So I give him grace for that.

‘The problem is that Yoro is not experienced. So if you’re going to bring in De Ligt, you’ve got to bring another experienced defender in with him.

‘If De Ligt is going to be there and Harry Maguire is there then it’s alright and if Maguire makes that mistake that Yoro made, I get it.

It has been revealed that ‘But Yoro is still young, he’s still learning the game. They’re both, to some extent, inexperienced at this moment in time so it’s the blind leading the blind.’.

United will look to stop the rot when they switch their focus to Champions League matters away to Sporting on Wednesday evening.

Three days later, Pochettino’s men return to Premier League action at home to Brentford.

Monza star Gustavo Varela has distanced himself from speculation that he could be set for a January transfer move and insists he is ‘paying no attention’ to incessant rumours linking him with Arsenal, Barcelona and Napoli.

Varela, 21, was deemed surplus to requirements at Benfica and completed a switch to newly promoted Italian outfit Monza for a fee of just €2million (£1.7m) – plus performance-related bonuses – in the summer.

It has proven a tough start to the season for Monza on their return to Serie A, with the club picking up just three wins and languishing down in 14th place in the table.

Varela has proven a shining light up front, though, scoring 11 goals in his opening 11 top-flight appearances, and the striker’s barnstorming form in Lombardy has begun to attract the attentions of European football’s elite.

According to recent reports emanating out of Varela’s native Portugal, Barca, Napoli and Arsenal are all actively pursuing a deal for the forward on the back of his goalscoring exploits in the first three months of the campaign.

Premier League champions Arsenal are mentioned to be among a host of Premier League clubs that have ‘expressed an interest’ in Varela and were ‘one of the first to enquire’ about the player’s potential availability.

It’s understood the Gunners are in the market for an attacker of Varela’s profile, with Viktor Gyokeres struggling to live up to expectations following his £64m arrival from Sporting last year.

On Monday night, Varela ensured he remained in the headlines with a terrific brace in Monza’s 3-0 victory over Fiorentina – in doing so, becoming only the third player in the last 50 years to reach the double figures in their first 11 Serie A games.

‘I can’t believe what I’m doing. I go home, close my eyes and I can’t believe it. Football is made of moments,’ Varela told DAZN Italy following Monza’s win.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

On his brilliant flicked effort to complete his double, Varela added: ‘It was pure instinct, it’s not something I practice.

‘A very beautiful cross came in, I was close to the goal and I decided to try my luck. If you don’t try, you can’t do it, and it happened.’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, varela was then asked for his reaction the rumoured interest he was receiving from some of Europe’s most high-profile teams, to which he responded: ‘I continue to thank Monza for allowing me to be here. It has all been incredible.

‘I feel lucky to be part of this reality and I only hope to continue on this path.

‘I pay no attention to the news. I only focus on what I have to do on the field. It’s normal, it’s part of football.

‘I’m going through a great moment but a less good moment may arise tomorrow.

Trust us, you're going to want to watch this OUTRAGEOUS finish from Gustavo Varela 😮‍💨🔥#MonzaFiorentina #UNROSSOALLAVIOLENZA pic.twitter.com/Z2RvJFul6X.

‘That’s why I try to simply enjoy the present without paying attention to the news.

‘Sometimes they speak well of me and sometimes they speak badly, but this is the world of football and I only think about what I have to do on the field.’.

Monza are believed to have slapped an asking price on Varela in the region of €40-50m (£33-42m).

Though they did not insert a buy-back clause in their deal with Monza for Varela, Benfica will be entitled to 20 per cent of any future transfer fee for the sought-after youngster.

The Primeira Liga club also have the right of first refusal should a bidding war break out for the Portugal Under-21 international, who was named the Serie A Rising Star of the Month for October.

Varela’s current contract with Monza runs through to June 2030.

Managers are neurotic creatures and Alonso’s great obsession is “control”, which you’d have to say is rather concerning from what we have seen of his tenure so far.

Recent findings suggest that ask the Spaniard to name his favourite performance from Chelsea’s opening 11 games of the Premier League season and he will cite last month’s 2-0 away win over Everton. A rare victory up north delivered a first top-flight clean sheet since January and, more importantly, was professional and diligent.

There is a time and a place for football as entertainment, but Alonso is in a results-based business and knows, from his unbeaten campaign leading Bayer Leverkusen to Bundesliga glory, that the less memorable wins are key to building a team in control of its destiny, delivering consistent results.

Chelsea are many things; they are not that.

The club were understandably excited in the summer when they secured their first-choice candidate, and appointing Alonso as manager, not head coach, has given the impression that he has more control in the overall running of first-team operations than his recent predecessors.

That is not translating to the pitch, though. Far from it. In every area of the field, control is absent without leave.

Four months in, Xabi Alonso is yet to imprint his identity on Chelsea.

Joao Pedro’s thigh injury has left Chelsea hamstrung in attack. Cole Palmer looks lost and ineffectual; Morgan Rogers is left carrying an excessive burden.

It has been revealed that the performances with and without another player, Moises Caicedo, are just as strikingly worlds apart from each other. An overreliance on the Ecuadorian has set alarm bells ringing for months.

The constant need for one midfielder to fill in alongside the centre-backs leaves Chelsea brutally outnumbered in the middle of the park, just as in the defeats by Brentford and Tottenham.

Both before and since Maxence Lacroix’s untimely injury, Alonso has been so unable to trust Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana that 20-year-old Josh Acheampong has proven the only broadly solid defender.

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal learn £100m twist; upcoming Man Utd target.

Fofana risks Chelsea fan fury as he laughs off criticism: ‘Couldn’t care less’.

Chelsea handed Joao Pedro warning ahead of £100m transfer decision.

Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style.

Chopping and changing between a back three and back four is merely a product of Alonso’s desperation to find a defensive unit that works, yet it has been an enemy to that search for control.

Chelsea have seen little of the ball in some games, but the early wins over Fulham and Brighton came through slick play in transition, and Alonso believes control is not just about slow and steady possession.

“We have spells where I would like us to have better control, and I’m not meaning just control with the ball,” he explained.

According to recent reports, “You can have control without the ball when you feel comfortable [because] you know the opponent has the ball where you want them to have it. Then you feel in control. That is the way I like to play.”.

Yet there remains a huge disparity between Alonso’s vision of control without the ball and Chelsea’s actual reality.

In a recent development, teams are consistently occupying the ball in very dangerous areas and creating the better chances. Leeds, for example, could have scored far more than four on Saturday.

Scoring 20 goals and conceding the same number doesn’t spell control, and it is the first time in a decade that Chelsea have lost as many as five of their opening 11 league fixtures.

Friday night against Nottingham Forest must be more like that mature win at Everton with less of the chaos seen from Chelsea since.

Alonso was considered the brightest new tactical mind in management less than two years ago, but is yet to imprint his identity on Chelsea four months in. He is not under immediate pressure of the sack, but grace periods don’t last forever.

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:37 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 04:38 EST, 24 November 2026.

Radja Nainggolan has claimed his former team-mate Romelu Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement on Belgian football following his shock retirement from the national team.

Lukaku, 33, unexpectedly announced his retirement from international football following Belgium's Nations League matches against Turkey and Italy earlier this month.

Belgium's all-time record goalscorer had been left on the bench against Italy, while he had not been in the squad three days earlier for the match against Turkey.

Lukaku's shock announcement caught Belgian media by surprise, while his former international team-mate Nainggolan has claimed more news will follow from the star.

Nainggolan, who won 30 caps for the national team between 2009 and 2018, revealed on the Ongefilterd Voetbal podcast he had a one-hour phone call with Lukaku following his decision.

The former Inter Milan and Roma midfielder stated that Lukaku told him: 'You are only allowed to say that a bombshell is about to explode.'.

Romelu Lukaku declared his shock retirement from international football earlier this month.

Sources indicate that former team-mate Radja Nainggolan claims Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement for Belgian football following a one hour phone call with the star. Source: Ongefilterd Voetbal.

'So something is still coming,' Nainggolan noted.

'What? I don't know. There were some internal problems between him and a certain person. But I'm not going to say much about that.

Industry observers note that 'Romelu will bring that up himself. He was a bit bitter, though. He was disappointed, frustrated.

'We will hear from him soon what will happen.

'About the real problems that were at play, he will be able to explain that better than I.'.

Lukaku's retirement had marked a stunning reversal of his looks, with the former Chelsea and Manchester United forward having vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament with the Belgium national team.

Describing his international career as a 'great ride', Lukaku had confirmed his international retirement on social media.

'16 years old', his Instagram statement began. 'For 16 years, I gave everything for the national team. I experienced every possible emotion. I played with fantastic teammates for whom I will always be grateful.

Lukaku vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament.

The Belgian forward has fallen down the pecking order and spent a lot of time on the bench.

According to recent reports, 'I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches for pushing me and giving me the confidence to help the team. It was a great ride, and I enjoyed every moment.

It has been revealed that 'To the Belgian fans, thank you for the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at four World Cups and three European Championships. I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing, it was a joy. I am grateful. Thank you.'.

The Belgian veteran accompanied his post with a gallery of photographs from his storied international career, from his debut against Croatia under Dick Advocaat in 2010 to his final chapter wearing the armband.

Lukaku has captained Belgium on a handful of occasions since 2020, alongside the likes of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans.

The 33-year-old forward, who became one of the hottest properties in world football after breaking onto the scene at Chelsea, has been a regular fixture in the international set-up for almost two decades.

Spearheading Belgium's golden generation, which included star-studded talents such as De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, Lukaku chalked up an impressive 135 caps for the international team.

He also retired as Belgium's all-time top scorer on 94 goals, just six shy of a century.

After suffering multiple injury setbacks, he featured at the 2026 World Cup under Rudi Garcia and continued to play a crucial role, scoring three times as a substitute to guide Belgium to the quarter-finals where they were ultimately stopped by eventual champions Spain.

Since Mark van Bommel's appointment in August, following Garcia's departure at the end of his contract, Lukaku has slipped further down the pecking order, with Charles De Ketelaere preferred to lead the line.

During Belgium's resounding 4-1 victory over Italy on Sunday, Lukaku warmed the bench as an unused substitute – and wasn't even in the squad to face Turkey three days before.

Lukaku, pictured with Kevin De Bruyne, was an unused substitute as Belgium beat Italy 4-1.

While Belgium were winning in the second half against the Italians, Lukaku was seen warming up on the sidelines in the hope of featuring for one last time, but unfortunately was not given the opportunity.

VTM NIEUWS anchor Maarten Breckx claimed De Bruyne looked 'concerned' while speaking to Lukaku on the bench, suggesting the former Man City star was unhappy to see his team-mate overlooked.

'When it became clear that he wouldn't be allowed to come on, De Bruyne was talking to him. You could see the concern in his eyes,' he said.

According to recent reports, 'You could tell, especially from Romelu's attitude, that he was dissatisfied and displeased. He had probably counted on getting some minutes...'.

With only Jan Vertonghen and Axel Witsel registering more international caps than Lukaku over their careers, boasting 157 and 140 appearances respectively, Belgium are expected to give the 33-year-old forward a send-off he deserves in the near future.

Witsel, who also called time on his Belgium career this year, was one of the team-mates to celebrate Lukaku's retirement on Instagram.

It has been revealed that 'Thanks for everything, legend. Thank you, what a journey we've had together,' he wrote.

Industry observers note that so far this season, he’s attempted only 16 dribbles at just over three per game, and has only succeeded on five. With one successful dribble per game on average, his success rate is just over 31% (FotMob data).

Rasmus Hojlund has revealed that Bruno Fernandes was among the Manchester United players to be left “devastated” by the recent sacking of Michael Carrick.

Carrick was relieved of his duties as Man Utd boss earlier in November after weeks of intense speculation and less than six months in permanent charge on a two-year contract, with just one win from their opening 10 games having seen his side languish in the Premier League relegation zone.

It is United’s worst start to a top-flight season since 1972, with former Chelsea and Tottenham manager Mauricio Pochettino leaving his role as head coach of the United States national team to quickly succeed Carrick, only to suffer a chastening 4-0 defeat by arch-rivals Liverpool with 10 men in his first match in charge.

Carrick’s final weeks at United saw senior players air their grievances in public interviews following listless defeats, with Lisandro Martinez taking aim at the club’s recruitment after the loss to Atletico Madrid and Fernandes then questioning Carrick’s tactics in the 4-1 thrashing away at Como.

However, captain and coach were stated to have held “clear-the-air talks” and been on good terms before the latter’s dismissal, with Hojlund revealing that Fernandes - along with United and Portugal team-mate Diogo Dalot - had been “devastated” by Carrick’s departure but hopeful of bouncing back promptly under his replacement.

The Danish striker was back in Manchester on Tuesday night in the Champions League, scoring for Napoli against City and making headlines with his pro-United celebration in a lively 2-2 draw at the Etihad Stadium.

Hojlund previously spent three years at Old Trafford between 2023-26 following a high-profile £72million transfer from Atalanta aged 20, netting 26 times in 95 total appearances across all competitions before returning to Serie A for £38m in the summer as Napoli exercised their option for a permanent deal following a successful season-long loan spell last term.

“In the international break when I spoke with Bruno and Diogo, they were all obviously devastated that Michael was going but also looking forward to some change,” said Hojlund, who recently scored twice for Denmark in their 4-1 thrashing of a Cristiano Ronaldo-less Portugal in the Nations League.

“I am still speaking with [Denmark team-mate and United player] Patrick [Dorgu] and I just wish the guys all the best and I am sure they will turn it around this season.”.

Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1176 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that in this plot of the Riemann ζ function on the complex plane, every point represents a complex number, with the real part plotted on the horizontal axis (from −10 to 10) and the imaginary part on the vertical axis (also from −10 to 10).
  • Recent findings suggest that in a year that has seen artificial intelligence reach one spectacular mathematical breakthrough after another, Anthropic has now claimed the top prize of them all: a full proof of the Riemann hypothesis, the statement that many mathematicians consider the most important open problem in the field.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that in this plot of the Riemann ζ function on the complex plane, every point represents a complex number, with the real part plotted on the horizontal axis (from −10 to 10) and the imaginary part on the vertical axis (also from −10 to 10). The colours represent the output of the function, with the junctions where the hues converge around a point showing some of the all-important zeroes.Credit: Empetrisor via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0).

Recent findings suggest that in a year that has seen artificial intelligence reach one spectacular mathematical breakthrough after another, Anthropic has now claimed the top prize of them all: a full proof of the Riemann hypothesis, the statement that many mathematicians consider the most important open problem in the field. But on the same day as the Anthropic claim, a separate study claiming to have proven the Riemann also emerged — and this one is entirely human written.

The Anthropic announcement came on 20 November from Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at the San Francisco, California, organization. “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge wrote, referring to Anthropic’s large language model (LLM).

AI is ‘the end of mathematics as we know it’ — where does the field go next?

AI is ‘the end of mathematics as we know it’ — where does the field go next?

“If this fully checks out, it is clearly a historic milestone in mathematics,” says number theorist James Maynard, a winner of the Fields Medal — mathematics’ most prestigious prize — at the University of Oxford, UK.

In a recent development, hours later, Ravi Vakil, a mathematician at Stanford University in California, posted a rival preprint to Alpöge’s online, in what Vakil called a “hurried announcement” of a proof that “is all human, with no AI”. The preprint was written by Alessandro Maria Masullo, a mathematician who received his PhD at Stanford in 2020 under the supervision of number theorist Brian Conrad. “The hope was to have Brian work with Alessandro for a year to polish the writing and then announce it after running it by enough people,” Vakil wrote. “Now it seems best to put out the current draft.”.

The confirmation of either or both solutions would be a spectacular bicentenary present for Bernhard Riemann, the German mathematician who was born 200 years ago this September and who formulated the problem, which addresses the distribution of prime numbers, in the mid-1800s.

According to recent reports, the Riemann hypothesis is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute, which has its scientific headquarters in Oxford, UK, at the turn of the twenty-first century. The institute offers a US$1 million prize to anyone who devises a solution to one of the problems, which are considered some of the most challenging in the field. Mathematicians using AI tools declared earlier this year that they had solved another Millennium problem, related to the Navier-Stokes equation.

It has been revealed that the problem has to do with the ‘Riemann ζ function’ (ζ is the Greek letter zeta), which encodes the randomness properties of the prime numbers. Riemann discovered that the distribution of primes is encoded in the ζ function’s ‘zeros’. These are points, denoted by z, on a plane satisfying the equation ζ(z) = 0.

Riemann conjectured that apart from some obvious but uninteresting cases, all such solutions had to lie on a certain vertical line in the plane. If this were true, he highlighted, it would imply that prime numbers are scattered among all whole numbers in a way that is essentially as random as it could be.

Sources indicate that the Riemann hypothesis has been a lodestar for generations of mathematicians. Credit: James Brittain/Getty.

Alpöge’s four-page document includes a sketch of the proof. But Andrew Granville, a number theorist at the University of Montreal in Canada, says that Alpöge should have taken the time to prepare a clearer write-up before making the announcement, which came just days after Anthropic’s initial public offering (IPO). The IPO initially valued the firm at US$1.5 trillion, but the company’s valuation dropped on 19 November.

“What he released is garbled,” Granville indicates of Alpöge’s document. Granville cites the downturn in the organization’s stock value as the reason for the timing of the proof’s release.

“There is an obvious cynical view, to do with the timing, but it is false,” Alpöge wrote in the document.

Anthropic did not respond immediately to Nature’s request for comment.

Industry observers note that tristan Buckmaster, a mathematician at Newly introduced York University who collaborated with Alpöge on a separate project regarding the Navier-Stokes equation, says that Alpöge deserves a lot of credit for developing techniques to produce mathematical results using LLMs. “Levent himself built this amazing set-up to do math.” He adds that Alpöge, who is himself a number theorist on leave from Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts, has been working relentlessly for months on this and other problems, hardly ever getting any sleep.

‘The job description is changing’: mathematician Terence Tao on the rise of AI.

‘The job description is changing’: mathematician Terence Tao on the rise of AI.

“I suspect that the proof will turn out to be correct,” Maynard says of the Alpöge announcement, even though it is now in the form of incomprehensible code in the Lean programming language.

While the Villans have lost three of their last six games in all competitions, they have drawn each of the previous Premier League games ahead of facing Ipswich Town this weekend.

According to recent reports, villa are unbeaten in their last seven league games (W3 D4), with each of their last three ending level. They last drew four consecutively in August/September 2011.

However, after their European defeat in Turkiye, Mings admitted it is on the players to turn their form around.

Recent findings suggest that "Everything is a collective responsibility. It's a real team effort," stated Mings.

"We're just trying to find, at the moment, our way, and trying to learn from the previous games, trying to do things that have given us success until now.

“At the moment, we're finding it in patches, but we’re not finding it consistently enough.

"We showed what we can do in patches, and that's not good enough when you come here and play at the top level.

"So, very frustrating, but it's on us to turn things around and to look at what we can do.".

"We knew there would be some tough days in here and we'll get ready to go again.

MATCH PREDICTION – ASTON VILLA WIN.

In a recent development, villa are unbeaten in their last 11 away league games against Ipswich (W5 D6), since a 3-0 loss in September 1984. In their league history, only at Coventry have they had a longer unbeaten run on the road (13 between 1938 and 1986).

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has stated that his future is presently "not crucial".

Fernandes, 32, only has a contract with the Red Devils until the end of the campaign, but the club do have the option to extend it for a further 12 months.

The Portugal international has reportedly rejected Man United's latest offer, allegedly wanting a longer deal with higher wages given his contribution during a tough period.

There is right now speculation surrounding his future at Old Trafford, but Fernandes has insisted that his main focus for the moment is on helping Man United to turn their campaign around.

"For us to start winning games and then we can talk about contract," Fernandes told reporters ahead of Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon, when asked what would need to happen for him to sign a new deal.

"It’s not important now. It’s my future, I haven’t got much left in my contract, but we will have time to speak about that. The conversations stopped when we thought now was not the moment.".

Fernandes also refused to "close the door" on returning to Sporting before the end of his career.

"I will never close the door to [returning to] Sporting. It will always be a club with a special place in my heart," the Man United captain added.

The Portuguese represented Sporting between 2017 and 2020 ahead of a move to Man United, scoring 63 goals and registering 50 assists in 137 appearances for the club.

Since arriving at Man United, Fernandes has a record of 113 goals and 111 assists in 342 appearances for the English team in all competitions.

Fernandes is again expected to be in the starting side when the Red Devils tackle Sporting in the league stage of the Champions League on Wednesday night.

The playmaker has six goals and three assists in 15 appearances in all competitions this season.

Meanwhile, Fernandes has a record of nine goals and 12 assists in 29 career appearances in the Champions League during his time at Sporting and Man United.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Aston Villa vs Manchester City.

Premier League leaders City will attempt to maintain their flawless start to the season when they visit Villa Park for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.

The match marks the first meeting between the sides since the final weekend of last season, when Villa secured a 2-1 victory at the Etihad in Pep Guardiola’s final game in charge at City.

In a recent development, enzo Maresca became the first manager in City’s Premier League history to win his opening seven fixtures, lifting his side three points clear of title holders Arsenal. Only Chelsea in 2005-06 and Liverpool in 2019-20 have managed a longer winning start to a top-flight campaign. Following a 3-2 victory against Ipswich Town last weekend, City rebounded from a European setback against Paris Saint-Germain by delivering a commanding 5-1 Champions League win over AEK Athens on Wednesday.

According to recent reports, however, Unai Emery’s side will present a formidable challenge. Aston Villa enter the contest on a seven-match unbeaten streak across all competitions, headlined by a perfect record in the Champions League following midweek success against Viking FK.

Villa’s domestic form has also improved, taking seven points from their last three league outings, including a 1-0 away victory at Newcastle United in Emery’s 100th Premier League match as manager. Sitting 12th in the table, Villa remain on the hunt for their first home league win of the season, though their impressive European performances at Villa Park provide significant momentum.

Emery’s men completed a league double over City last term, including a 1-0 win on home turf. Should Villa claim victory again on Saturday, it would mark the first time in the Premier League era that they have recorded three consecutive victories over the Manchester club.

Of course, City’s campaign remains overshadowed by the recent guilty verdict from the Premier League over financial regulations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unai Emery delivered a blunt assessment of Alejandro Garnacho’s situation at Aston Villa after the Argentine was left out of the squad for the defeat to Galatasaray on Tuesday night.

Villa were beaten 1-0 in Turkey and now sit ninth in the Champions League table, one place outside the automatic qualification spots.

Garnacho, meanwhile, trained with his Villa teammates on Monday but he was not even named on the bench against Galatasaray.

The on-loan Chelsea winger was also not included in Villa’s squad for their goalless draw at home to Sunderland on Saturday.

For the game against Galatasaray, Emery only picked 11 substitutes out of a possible 12 and also included two goalkeepers.

When asked about Garnacho’s absence after Villa’s defeat, Emery replied: ‘Today the players were here who I think are the best players to be here with us, to play with us.’.

Garnacho has made just seven appearances since joining Villa in the summer and is yet to score a goal or register an assist.

Villa have an obligation to buy Garnacho from Chelsea for £43 million but only if he makes a certain number of appearances this season.

Chelsea signed Garnacho in a £40m deal from Manchester United last year but the Argentine struggled to make an impact during his time at Stamford Bridge, scoring eight goals in 43 appearances.

Viktor Gyokeres has warned of the obvious threat that Manchester City still pose to Arsenal ahead of their huge showdown this weekend.

The Premier League title rivals lock horns in north London on Sunday afternoon, with six points and two places separating them in the table as things stand.

Defending champions Arsenal have won nine of their first 11 top-flight games this season to already sit six points clear at the summit following a dramatic 2-2 draw at Newcastle, while they remain unbeaten in the Champions League.

That is in stark contrast to City, who sit third behind surprise package Brighton after Saturday’s disappointing home draw with Fulham, which came after back-to-back surprise losses at the hands of Brighton and Nottingham Forest.

Those struggles continued in the Champions League on Tuesday night, when Enzo Maresca’s side twice had to fight back from a deficit to claim a 2-2 home draw with Napoli - after which star striker Erling Haaland expressed concern over their lack of wins.

Despite that disappointing form, Gyokeres believes that City will still present a significant challenge to Arsenal in their blockbuster clash at the Emirates Stadium this weekend.

“They still have a very good squad and very good players,” the Swedish forward mentioned after scoring the opening goal in Arsenal’s 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday.

“Sometimes, you may have a period where you don’t get the results all the time – which is normal for any club.

“It is going to be a difficult game on Sunday. But it is always fun with major games. It is going to be good.”.

Gyokeres insists that Arsenal will not spend any time thinking about the potentially significant ramifications of City’s Premier League charges on this season’s title race.

In September, an independent commission found City guilty of all charges related to alleged serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules across a nine-season period between 2009/10 and 2017/18 in a seismic verdict.

Recent findings suggest that no sanctions against City have yet been revealed, with the club appealing the decision. They deny any wrongdoing.

The latest reports suggest that City’s appeal could be heard in December, with a potential ruling expected early in 2027.

“It is what it is,” Gyokeres mentioned of the situation, per the Press Association. “We are focused on the game on Sunday.

Industry observers note that “We can’t control that. It has nothing to do with us. So, we don’t put any energy into that.”.

  • Manchester United need to show character as they attempt to bounce back in Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon, ex-Red Devils midfielder Gordon Strachan has exclusively told Sports Mole.
  • The 20-time English champions will enter the European fixture with Sporting off the back of a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 20:30, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 20:31.

Manchester United need to show character as they attempt to bounce back in Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon, ex-Red Devils midfielder Gordon Strachan has exclusively told Sports Mole.

The 20-time English champions will enter the European fixture with Sporting off the back of a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in the Premier League.

Mauricio Pochettino will now take charge of his first European match for Man United, and there is pressure on the Argentine following the four-goal mauling at Anfield.

When asked whether the Sporting match provided Man United with the perfect chance to bounce back from the defeat to Liverpool, Strachan insisted that the players need to show character and heart in a bid to turn the club's campaign around.

"Well, to be fair, Liverpool should never really be a major ask for Man United as such, because the record there is terrific over the years. I mean, it's always been decent. That fixture is one of the ones that Liverpool really want to win because they know how dangerous Man United are," remarked Strachan.

Industry observers note that "But it wasn't a real game after the first two goals, there was the sending-off, you know. And even the free kick, you think, right, if you see the free kick off, we can reorganise and organise with 10 players. We never even had time to do that. So, as a manager, you can't count that, you've just got to count that as a no-game.

"But what you can do in that situation is ask, who kept pressing? Who do I want in my team? Because in adversity, you see the real character coming out, and in adversity in substantial games, you see the real character. And it's not on your social media, it's not saying to the fans, we love you and we're sorry and all the rest of it. Don't apologise to me, just do something about it.

"Don't come in and hold your hand up and say, I'm sorry, gaffer. Don't apologise to me because I'm not interested in you telling me you're sorry for making a mistake. Just don't make a mistake. And if you do make a mistake, rectify it as promptly as possible.

"What I'm talking about is managers will try and sort it out. Invariably, unless you can do something about it, physically or mentally, then it will appear again. They will appear, and they'll appear in crisis moments.

It has been revealed that "As I said, your character is shown up in crisis times and the same mistakes will be made by the same people whoever they play. And some people are just not good enough to play at this level.

It has been revealed that "You know, we all talk about shapes and systems and this and that. The funny thing is, I don't think there's too many people talking about systems now. I think most people are now talking about, even if you talk with a bright manager, they talk about putting people under pressure, winning knockdowns, getting to the ball first, getting the ball to your front men.

"So, the system thing has kind of changed now. The only one that kind of really changes, it's gone from a back four to a back three, but the rest, like Brighton, Liverpool, Bournemouth, they're all playing the same sort of way.

According to recent reports, "It's a kind of 4-2-3-1, where the four players up front are attacking players, whatever way you want to use it, two wide men, just off the front. Wales were the same with Craig Bellamy.

"So, I think that people are moving to that in general now, but there's not too much talking about systems now. It's more about closing down, getting to knockdowns, winning headers and free kicks and corner kicks.".

Man United have six points to show from their two matches in the league stage of this season's Champions League.

Gordon Strachan was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of William Hill Football Odds.

It remains to be seen whether De Ligt will play again in Lisbon, with Harry Maguire introduced in the first half at Anfield following Yoro’s dismissal.

Maguire should start against Sporting, perhaps alongside Yoro, who would have been available in Europe regardless of United’s appeal being successful or not.

That could see Lisandro Martinez plugged in at left-back once more if Shaw is not ready to start, although the Argentine had to shift inside after Yoro’s red card against Liverpool, with Patrick Dorgu then moving back.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 05:07 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 05:13 EST, 24 November 2026.

Premier League clubs are bracing themselves for a new raid of their talent from Saudi Arabia, as the mega-money league considers relaxing spending rules.

Teams in the Saudi Pro League (SPL) are currently only allowed eight foreign players in their 25-man squads but are discussing increasing that number to 14 or even higher.

If the move is approved, it is likely to trigger a flood of cash in the market similar to the massive £765million spree in 2023 that saw the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Karim Benzema and N'Golo Kante sign for Public Investment Fund (PIF) teams.

In that 2023 window, almost half of the transfer fees received by Premier League clubs came from the SPL.

In total, 94 players were signed by Pro League clubs and the January transfer window could now follow a similar pattern.

The Saudi spending reached such astronomic levels that it eclipsed every other league in Europe aside from the Premier League.

Cristiano Ronaldo (right) and Angelo, pictured in action for Al Nassr, are among the foreign stars already plying their trade in Saudi Arabia and more will be on their way.

The supposed reason for the proposed rule change is to elevate the standard of existing Saudi players at home by raising the overall level of talent ahead of the country hosting the World Cup in 2034.

But critics argue that the new rules would only force Saudi players out of their domestic league in place of high-profile foreign recruits.

While Premier League clubs are often reluctant to allow talent to leave in January midway through the season, the fees on offer from Saudi can be eye-watering and hard to turn down.

Aston Villa sold Jhon Duran and later Ollie Watkins for a combined £115million to the SPL.

Fulham accepted £50m for Aleksandar Mitrovic, while Wolves banked £47m for Ruben Neves and Liverpool were able to recoup almost £50m for Darwin Nunez.

West Ham were able to cash in on Crysencio Summerville after relegation last term when Al Hilal bought him for £60m.

Would Man United consider offers for Bruno Fernandes as his contract winds down? Or will they keep the club captain to help battle relegation?

Suddenly every Premier League club recruitment department will be reassessing their squads and be keeping a close eye on the rule developments in Saudi.

Ollie Watkins moved from Aston Villa to Al Hilal and the Premier League side have recouped huge fees from the SPL in the  past.

Ivan Toney (second from left) and his Al Ahli team-mates celebrate a goal against Al Nassr.

The SPL's decision on whether to allow the increase of foreign players will be clarified before the winter window opens.

The PIF are winding down their investment in golf through LIV having invested more than £3.7billion since 2021 but their operation in football reveals no sign of slowing down.

Players weighing up a move to Saudi will perhaps have a more difficult decision than in 2023 over relocating, with conflict still affecting the country.

The Asian Cup was postponed earlier in November following a missile attack from Yemen-based Houthi rebels on Riyadh airport that killed 13 people and injured more than 300.

Security fears and geo-political uncertainty could make footballers think twice before accepting the lucrative contracts on offer in January and beyond.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Chelsea and England star Shaun Wright-Phillips has urged Estevao to fight tooth and nail for a starting spot at Stamford Bridge and make himself ‘hard to ignore’ under Xabi Alonso.

Estevao burst onto the scene across an eye-catching opening campaign with Chelsea having joined the club from Palmeiras in the summer of 2025, racking up eight goals and four assists for the Blues.

A serious hamstring tear brought Estevao’s debut season to a premature end, though, a devastating blow that saw him miss out on a place in Brazil’s squad at this year’s World Cup.

Just days after Estevao sustained his injury, Chelsea decided to call time on Liam Rosenior’s turbulent managerial spell – and it has proven difficult for the 19-year-old to work himself back into the side since Alonso took charge.

The teenager had been limited to only two starts in the Carabao Cup approaching late October and rumours were beginning to circulate that he had grown frustrated with his peripheral role, with Barcelona reportedly keeping tabs on the situation.

However, Joao Pedro’s absence over the last month-and-a-half has created an opportunity for Estevao in Alonso’s attack and the youngster has started two of Chelsea’s last three games.

A humbling 4-1 defeat at the hands of Leeds may not have been what Estevao had in mind for his return, though, following a substitute appearance at Sunderland, and he will no doubt be desperate to banish those memories with a strong performance versus Nottingham Forest on Friday night.

Asked if he felt that Estevao still had a big future at Chelsea under Alonso, Wright-Phillips told Metro, courtesy of kwiff: ‘It’s a hard one, because it seems like players at Chelsea outlive the managers, which is sad to say.

Industry observers note that ‘That’s where modern football is going at the minute. It seems like players are outlasting coaches.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘But in general, that’s more of a tactical thing, in that Xabi plays more with wing-backs.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

‘If you play Estevao, you want him in the front three. Chances come in random ways, so he will get his chance again, and he has to do what he did the other day.

Recent findings suggest that ‘When he came on, I thought he was flying: not the weekend just gone, the weekend before that [against Sunderland. He came on and played really, really well.

‘So that’s him saying, “Look, I’m good enough to stay in your squad.” If he continuously does that, it becomes hard to ignore.’.

Another player whose development has hit something of a stumbling block in recent months is Malo Gusto, who, like Estevao, has found regular game-time hard to come by this season.

Reports just last week indicated Gusto could be open to the prospect of leaving Chelsea, with Manchester United understood to be among the right-back’s admirers.

Recent findings suggest that but when asked if it could be time to move Gusto on should a suitable offer come in for the Frenchman, Wright-Phillips replied: ‘Who do you replace him with? I think Gusto is a really fantastic player.

‘He might not be happy, which is understandable, because before Xabi came, when the other managers were there, his playing time was a lot greater, because it was either him or Reece James.

It has been revealed that ‘Reece James has had bad luck, he’s injured quite a lot, so Gusto got to play a lot. Whereas now, I think he’s better than a bit-part player, to be honest.

‘I haven’t watched him enough this season to turn around and say he should definitely be starting, but from what I saw of him last year and the type of player he is, I’d have him in my team at the drop of a hat, because I don’t think there are many right-backs out there that are gettable of that standard.’.

Chelsea splashed out in the region of £350million on upcoming signings in the summer transfer window, including Morgan Rogers, who commanded a club-record fee of £117m when he joined from Aston Villa.

There were signs that the Blues were reaping the rewards of their substantial spending in a promising start to the 2026/27 campaign, with Alonso’s all-star front three firing on all cylinders.

An injury to Joao Pedro has coincided with a concerning dip in results, though, and Alonso’s men were targeted with a chorus of boos as they exited the pitch following their latest setback on Saturday.

‘I think at the very beginning he highlighted why he’s there, and at the minute it seems to have plateaued a bit. I don’t know what that’s from,’ Wright-Phillips said when asked what he had made of Alonso’s start to managerial life in the Premier League, with Chelsea languishing down in eighth.

‘Playing as many games as they have, with the internationals that have come in the way they’ve come in, it feels like the Champions League is every week; it feels like it’s the Carabao Cup or something every week at the minute.

‘It’s going to take a bit of time for the players to get used to that change, where every game is a massive game now for everybody; literally every game comes around very quick.

‘I think those clubs will settle down and get it together because they’re lucky to have the players within that squad to do that.’.

According to recent reports, pressed on whether there were any areas of the squad in need of strengthening in January, Wright-Phillips responded: ‘I’m not sure they need midfielders. I would say if they had two, or even one, solid defenders who can teach the other young ones there, that would be more than enough.

‘Chelsea have got an amazing squad. They’re missing that rock at the back; who will fight and die for everybody, because that rubs off on the team.

‘You might not like him, but that attitude and mentality will naturally rub off on you. Someone in the Thiago Silva mould.

Sources indicate that ‘They need to learn; they’re learning from each other. They’re good players, but to get to the top, most younger players and defenders learn off somebody with a lot more experience.’.

Switching his focus to the title race, Wright-Phillips, who represented Manchester City, Chelsea and QPR during his playing days, picked out Brighton as this year’s surprise package.

And while they were beaten in stoppage time by Hull City at the weekend, the ex-England winger is confident the Seagulls remain one of Arsenal’s ‘main challengers’.

‘No disrespect to Arsenal, but the best club for me in the Premier League this season, to watch and for output, is Brighton,’ Wright-Phillips – a Premier League winner with Chelsea in 2006 – explained.

‘Brighton are probably playing the best, but they’re not at the top of the league.

In a recent development, ‘It can change and go a different way. I don’t think Arsenal are playing that well, and I don’t think City have played that well, but they’re the two teams that know how to get results when they aren’t playing to the level they know their maximum is.

‘Unfortunately for City, that hasn’t happened in the last four games, which is something they have to deal with and turn around.

‘The Christmas period is the right time to possibly do it, because all the games come quick and fast and the league table can change a dozen times in that time.

Recent findings suggest that ‘The main challengers to Arsenal would be Brighton and Manchester City as it stands. They’re the ones with the points on the board.

‘Until people start putting the points on the board, which is turning around, you’re seeing Liverpool sneak back up the table.

‘There will be other challenges as well, but leading into this Christmas period, I would say Arsenal’s challenger right now is Brighton and Manchester City.

‘Brighton, I think, are the only team to beat both of those two teams and do it nicely as well. It wasn’t a smash and grab.’.
